### sec_appendix.tex
\begin{definition}[Multi-axis dynamic structure]\label{def:multi-axis-dynamic-structure}
Fix a model $M$. A \emph{multi-axis dynamic structure} on $M$ is a tuple
\[
\mathfrak{D}=\bigl(\St(M),\le,\tau,J,\{\rightsquigarrow_j\}_{j\in J}\bigr),
\]
where $J$ is an axis set, each $\rightsquigarrow_j$ is a single-axis advancement relation satisfying
\[
p\rightsquigarrow_j q \Longrightarrow q\le p,
\]
and $\tau:\St(M)\to T$ maps states to a linearly ordered set $T$ such that
\[
p\rightsquigarrow_j q \Longrightarrow \tau(q)\ge \tau(p).
\]
For finite $K\subseteq J$, write $p\rightsquigarrow_K q$ if $q$ is reachable from $p$ by a finite chain of advancements using only axes in $K$.
\end{definition}

### sec_appendix.tex
\begin{definition}[Delayed decidability]\label{def:delayed-decidability}
Let $p\rightsquigarrow_K q$. We say that $\varphi$ undergoes \emph{delayed decidability} from $p$ to $q$ if
\[
M,p\nVdash\varphi,\qquad
M,p\nVdash\neg\varphi,\qquad
\text{but}\qquad
M,q\Downarrow\varphi.
\]
\end{definition}

### sec_appendix.tex
\begin{definition}[Axis-information maps]\label{def:axis-information-maps}
Fix a multi-axis dynamic structure $\mathfrak{D}$ on a model $M$. For each axis $j\in J$, assume there is a finite set $I_j$ and a map
\[
\mathrm{info}_j:\{q\in\St(M)\mid p\rightsquigarrow_K q\text{ for some finite }K\ni j\}\longrightarrow I_j.
\]
For states $q$ and $r$ reachable from $p$ via $K$-advancements and a subset $L\subseteq K$, we say that $q$ and $r$ \emph{agree on $L$-information} if
\[
\mathrm{info}_j(q)=\mathrm{info}_j(r)
\qquad
\text{for every }j\in L.
\]
\end{definition}

### sec_appendix.tex
\begin{definition}[Support and minimal support]\label{def:axis-support}
Let $K\subseteq J$ be finite. We say that $K$ \emph{supports} a formula $\varphi$ at $p$, written $K\triangleright_p\varphi$, if whenever
\[
p\rightsquigarrow_K q,\qquad
p\rightsquigarrow_K r,
\]
and both $q$ and $r$ decide $\varphi$, agreement of the $K$-information (in the sense of \Cref{def:axis-information-maps}) implies agreement of the decision. A supporting set $K$ is \emph{minimal} if no proper subset of $K$ still supports $\varphi$ at $p$.
\end{definition}

### sec_appendix.tex
\begin{definition}[Indispensability]\label{def:axis-indispensability}
Let $K\subseteq J$ be finite and let $j\in K$. We say that $j$ is \emph{indispensable relative to $K$} for $\varphi$ at $p$ if there exist states $q$ and $r$ with
\[
p\rightsquigarrow_K q,\qquad
p\rightsquigarrow_K r,
\]
such that $q$ and $r$ agree on $(K\setminus\{j\})$-information (in the sense of \Cref{def:axis-information-maps}), while
\[
M,q\Vdash\varphi
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
M,r\Vdash\neg\varphi.
\]
\end{definition}

### sec_appendix.tex
\begin{definition}[Orthogonality]\label{def:axis-orthogonality}
Two axes $j,k\in J$ are \emph{orthogonal at $p$} if whenever
\[
p\rightsquigarrow_j q
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
p\rightsquigarrow_k r,
\]
there exists a state $u$ such that
\[
p\rightsquigarrow_{\{j,k\}} u,
\qquad
u\le q,
\qquad
u\le r.
\]
\end{definition}

### sec_appendix.tex
\begin{definition}[Fusion state and axis completeness]\label{def:fusion-state}
Let $K\subseteq J$ be finite, and suppose that for each $j\in K$ there is a single-axis refinement $p\rightsquigarrow_j q_j$. A state $u$ is a \emph{fusion state} for the family $(q_j)_{j\in K}$ if
\[
p\rightsquigarrow_K u
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
u\le q_j\ \text{for every }j\in K.
\]
The dynamic structure is \emph{axis-complete} if every finite pairwise orthogonal family of single-axis refinements admits a fusion state.
\end{definition}

### sec_appendix.tex
\begin{definition}[Value-preserving rewrite]\label{def:value-preserving-rewrite}
A \emph{readout expression} is any term whose semantic role at a state is determined by a typed readout. A rewrite
\[
E\leadsto E'
\]
between readout expressions is \emph{value preserving} if for every state $p$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item $\Read_p(E)$ is defined if and only if $\Read_p(E')$ is defined,
\item whenever defined, $\Read_p(E)=\Read_p(E')$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{definition}

### sec_appendix.tex
\begin{definition}[Amplitude lift of a support presheaf]\label{def:amplitude-lift}
Let $S_e$ be the support presheaf of a finite empirical model on a measurement-cover site $\mathcal C_a$. An \emph{amplitude lift} of $S_e$ with band $\Band$ is a realization prestack
\[
\mathfrak P_e\to \mathcal C_a
\]
together with an identification
\[
\pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_e)\cong S_e.
\]
Equivalently, an amplitude lift is a choice of local realization objects and phase-sensitive transition isomorphisms whose isomorphism classes recover the supported local assignments.
\end{definition}

### sec_branch_aggregation.tex
\begin{definition}[Branchwise intrinsic data]\label{def:branchwise-intrinsic-data}
Fix an admitted reference $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ at a state $p$, and assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item the hypotheses of \Cref{def:cech-gluing-obstruction} hold;
\item the set $\Vis_{p,s}(r)$ is finite and nonempty;
\item every component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ is banded by the same finite abelian group $A$ and admits a finite nerve presentation of its branch obstruction class $\omega_v$.
\end{enumerate}
For each visible branch $v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)$, write
\[
K_v:=K_{\omega_v},
\qquad
A_{\mathrm{vis}}^v:=A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\omega_v}=A/K_v,
\qquad
\pi_v:A\twoheadrightarrow A_{\mathrm{vis}}^v.
\]
\end{definition}

### sec_branch_aggregation.tex
\begin{definition}[Branch comparison map and resolution kernel]\label{def:branch-comparison-map}
In the setting of \Cref{def:branchwise-intrinsic-data}, let
\[
\pi_{\mathrm{br}}:A\twoheadrightarrow A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{br}}(r)
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\pi_{\mathrm{unif}}:A\twoheadrightarrow A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{unif}}(r)
\]
be the canonical quotient maps. Since
\[
\bigcap_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v
\subseteq
\sum_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v,
\]
there is a unique surjective homomorphism
\[
\beta_r:A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{br}}(r)\twoheadrightarrow A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{unif}}(r)
\]
such that
\[
\beta_r\circ \pi_{\mathrm{br}}=\pi_{\mathrm{unif}}.
\]
Its kernel is denoted
\[
B_{\mathrm{res}}(r):=
\ker(\beta_r)
\cong
\Bigl(\sum_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v\Bigr)\Big/\Bigl(\bigcap_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v\Bigr)
\]
and called the \emph{branch-resolution kernel}.
\end{definition}

### sec_branch_aggregation.tex
\begin{definition}[Branch-resolution code]\label{def:branch-resolution-code}
In the setting of \Cref{def:branch-comparison-map}, a \emph{branch-resolution code} consists of a finite set $R$ and an injective map
\[
\iota_{\mathrm{res}}:A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{br}}(r)\hookrightarrow A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{unif}}(r)\times R
\]
such that
\[
\mathrm{pr}_1\circ \iota_{\mathrm{res}}=\beta_r.
\]
\end{definition}

### sec_branch_aggregation.tex
\begin{definition}[Branch-preserving strictification code]\label{def:branch-preserving-strictification-code}
In the setting of \Cref{def:branchwise-intrinsic-data}, a \emph{branch-preserving strictification code} consists of a finite set $R$ and, for each visible branch $v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)$, an injective map
\[
\iota_v:A\hookrightarrow A_{\mathrm{vis}}^v\times R
\]
such that
\[
\mathrm{pr}_1\circ \iota_v=\pi_v.
\]
\end{definition}

### sec_gerbe_obstruction.tex
\begin{definition}[\v{C}ech--derived comparison package]\label{def:cech-derived-comparison-package}
For an admitted reference \(r:\mathsf{Ref}_s\) at \(p\), a band \(\Band\)
on \(\mathcal C_{p,s}/a\), and a visible branch \(v\), a
\emph{\v{C}ech--derived comparison package} consists of a filtered cofinal
family
\[
\Cov_v^{\mathrm{acyc}}(a)\subseteq \Cov_{p,s}(a)
\]
such that every cover \(\mathcal U=\{U_i\to a\}\) in the family has a
\v{C}ech nerve in the slice site, trivializes the band on all intersections
used in degrees \(0,1,2\), and satisfies the following comparison condition:
the canonical refinement map
\[
\varinjlim_{\mathcal U\in\Cov_v^{\mathrm{acyc}}(a)}
\check H^2(\mathcal U,\Band)
\longrightarrow
H^2(\mathcal C_{p,s}/a,\Band)
\]
is an isomorphism. One way to verify this condition is the usual Leray
hypothesis: all nonempty finite intersections appearing in the family are
\(\Band\)-acyclic in every positive degree needed for the derived
comparison. The definition itself, however, records the comparison
isomorphism as the required assumption; the later theorems do not silently
infer derived \(H^2\) from a single \v{C}ech cocycle unless this package, or
the explicit finite good-cover Leray theorem of
\Cref{lem:generated-subsite-model-interface}, is in force.
\end{definition}

### sec_gerbe_obstruction.tex
\begin{definition}[Component gerbes and branch obstruction classes]\label{def:compatible-realization-stack}\label{def:cech-gluing-obstruction}
Fix an admitted reference $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ at a state $p$, write
\[
a=[r]_p,
\]
and assume that $r$ admits a realization prestack $\mathfrak P_r$ with stackification $\mathfrak L_r$ and band $\Band$ as in \Cref{def:realization-prestack}. For a visible value class
\[
v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)\cong \pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a),
\]
let $\mathfrak G_v(U)$ be the full subgroupoid of $\mathfrak L_r(U)$ on those objects whose connected-component class restricts to $v$ on $U$. When \Cref{thm:component-gerbe-decomposition} applies, we call $\mathfrak G_v$ the \emph{component gerbe} of the visible branch $v$.

Assume moreover that \textup{(H4)} holds. For each visible branch $v$ and each cover
\[
\mathcal U\in \Cov_v^{\mathrm{acyc}}(a),
\]
\Cref{thm:cech-bridge-compatible-realizations} produces a \v{C}ech obstruction class
\[
[g_{\mathcal U}]\in \check H^2(\mathcal U,\Band).
\]
Refinement compatibility identifies these classes in the filtered system, and the comparison isomorphism in \textup{(H4)} therefore determines a unique derived class
\[
\omega_v\in H^2(\mathcal C_{p,s}/a,\Band),
\]
called the \emph{branch obstruction class} of $v$.
\end{definition}

### sec_gerbe_obstruction.tex
\begin{definition}[Banded realization-stack extension]\label{def:realization-stack-extension}
For an admitted reference $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ at a state $p$, abbreviate
\[
a=[r]_p,
\qquad
\mathcal C_a:=\mathcal C_{p,s}/a,
\]
and fix an abelian sheaf $\Band$ on $\mathcal C_a$. Let $\mathfrak E_r$ be a
$\Band$-banded stack in groupoids on $\mathcal C_a$. A
\emph{$\Band$-banded realization-stack extension} is a pair
\[
(\mathfrak E_r,\epsilon_r)
\]
consisting of such a stack together with an isomorphism of sheaves
\[
\epsilon_r:\pi_0(\mathfrak E_r)\xrightarrow{\sim} a_{p,s}F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}
\]
on $\mathcal C_a$.

For a visible value class
\[
v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)\cong \bigl(a_{p,s}F_{p,s}\bigr)(a),
\]
the \emph{$v$-component substack} of $\mathfrak E_r$ is the full substack
\[
\mathfrak E_r[v](U):=
\bigl\{x\in \mathfrak E_r(U)\mid \epsilon_{r,U}([x])=v|_U\bigr\}
\]
for objects $U$ of $\mathcal C_a$, where $\epsilon_{r,U}$ denotes the component of $\epsilon_r$ at $U$.
\end{definition}

### sec_gerbe_visible_strictification.tex
\begin{definition}[Ordered \v{C}ech convention]\label{def:ordered-cech-convention}
For every finite cover
\[
\mathcal U=\{a_i\to a\}_{i\in I}
\]
used in a finite obstruction presentation, fix a total order on $I$. The
group $\check C^n(\mathcal U,A)$ is indexed by strictly increasing
nondegenerate tuples
\[
i_0<\cdots<i_n
\]
whose overlap $a_{i_0\cdots i_n}$ is nonempty. If a value is written on an
arbitrary ordered tuple, it denotes the alternating extension from the
increasing tuple: permuting pairwise distinct indices multiplies the value
by the sign of the permutation, and a tuple with a repeated index has value
$0$. In degree $2$, the cocycle identity on every ordered nondegenerate
quadruple is
\[
\alpha_{jkl}-\alpha_{ikl}+\alpha_{ijl}-\alpha_{ijk}=0.
\]
Thus reversing the orientation of a nondegenerate triple replaces
$\alpha_{ijk}$ by $-\alpha_{ijk}$.
\end{definition}

### sec_gerbe_visible_strictification.tex
\begin{definition}[Finite obstruction presentation]\label{def:finite-obstruction-presentation}
Fix an admitted reference $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ at a state $p$, and assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item the hypotheses of \Cref{def:cech-gluing-obstruction} hold;
\item a visible branch
\[
v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)
\]
has been chosen;
\item the associated branch gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ is banded by a finite abelian group $A$,
\item a finite covering family
\[
\mathcal U=\{a_i\to a\}_{i\in I},
\qquad
a=[r]_p,
\]
has been chosen together with a \v{C}ech $2$-cocycle
\[
\alpha=(\alpha_{ijk})\in Z^2(\mathcal U,A)
\]
representing the branch obstruction class $\omega_v$, written in the ordered
convention of \Cref{def:ordered-cech-convention}.
\end{enumerate}
Define the \emph{obstruction subgroup}
\[
H_\alpha:=\langle \alpha_{ijk}\mid i<j<k\text{ and }a_{ijk}\neq\varnothing\rangle\le A,
\]
and the associated \emph{visible quotient}
\[
A_{\mathrm{vis}}:=A/H_\alpha.
\]
\end{definition}

### sec_gerbe_visible_strictification.tex
\begin{definition}[Coboundary action and presentation-invariant character channels]\label{def:gauge-invariance-character}
In the setting of \Cref{def:finite-obstruction-presentation}, the \v{C}ech $1$-cochain group $C^1(\mathcal U,A)$ acts on cocycles by coboundary translation: a cochain
\[
h=(h_{ij})\in C^1(\mathcal U,A)
\]
sends a cocycle $\alpha$ to the cohomologous cocycle
\[
(h\cdot\alpha)_{ijk}:=\alpha_{ijk}+(\delta h)_{ijk}.
\]
A character $\chi\in\widehat A$ is called \emph{presentation-invariant} for the chosen obstruction presentation if it kills the obstruction subgroup $H_\alpha$, equivalently if it factors through the quotient
\[
\pi:A\twoheadrightarrow A_{\mathrm{vis}}=A/H_\alpha.
\]
In that case the pushed-forward class $\chi_*[\alpha]$ depends only on the visible quotient and not on the chosen local trivializations.
\end{definition}

### sec_gerbe_visible_strictification.tex
\begin{definition}[Auxiliary strictification code]\label{def:auxiliary-strictification-code}
In the setting of \Cref{def:finite-obstruction-presentation}, an \emph{auxiliary strictification code} consists of a finite set $R$ and an injective map
\[
\iota:A\hookrightarrow A_{\mathrm{vis}}\times R
\]
such that the first projection recovers the canonical quotient:
\[
\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\iota=\pi.
\]
Equivalently, the visible quotient is kept fixed, while the auxiliary register $R$ resolves the hidden information inside the fibers of $\pi$.
\end{definition}

### sec_homological_visibility.tex
\begin{definition}[Finite nerve presentation of the obstruction class]\label{def:finite-nerve-presentation}
Fix an admitted reference $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ at a state $p$, and assume conditions \textup{(i)}--\textup{(iv)} of \Cref{def:finite-obstruction-presentation}, with the ordered \v{C}ech convention of \Cref{def:ordered-cech-convention}. A \emph{finite nerve presentation} of the branch obstruction class consists of:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item a finite covering family
\[
\mathcal U=\{a_i\to a\}_{i\in I},
\qquad
a=[r]_p,
\]
whose \v{C}ech nerve $N(\mathcal U)$ is finite;
\item a trivialization of the band on $\mathcal U$, so that the band may be viewed as a constant coefficient finite abelian group $A$ on $N(\mathcal U)$;
\item the induced finite-nerve class
\[
\omega\in H^2(N(\mathcal U),A),
\]
obtained by identifying \v{C}ech cochains on $\mathcal U$ with simplicial cochains on the finite nerve, transporting the branch obstruction cocycle through that identification, and writing
\[
\omega:=\omega_v
\]
for the chosen visible branch. When the class is also viewed as a derived
$H^2$-class, the presentation includes either the
\v{C}ech--derived comparison package of
\Cref{def:cech-derived-comparison-package} or the finite good-cover Leray
comparison of \Cref{lem:generated-subsite-model-interface}. Without one of
these comparison inputs, \(\omega\) is only the selected finite-nerve
\v{C}ech/simplicial class.
\end{enumerate}
Write
\[
\eta_A:H^2(N(\mathcal U),A)\longrightarrow \mathrm{Hom}(H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),A)
\]
for the map in the universal coefficient exact sequence
\[
0\to \operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),A)\to H^2(N(\mathcal U),A)\xrightarrow{\eta_A}\mathrm{Hom}(H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),A)\to 0
\]
\cite[Sec.~3.1]{Hatcher2002}, and define the \emph{homological evaluation map}
\[
\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}:=\eta_A(\omega).
\]
\end{definition}

### sec_homological_visibility.tex
\begin{definition}[Finite nerve comparison groupoid]\label{def:finite-nerve-comparison-relation}
For finite nerve presentations of a fixed branch obstruction class, an
\emph{elementary comparison} is one of the three operations listed in
\Cref{prop:invariance-visible-quotients}: homology-equivalent refinement,
cohomologous cocycle replacement, or re-trivialization of the constant band.
The \emph{finite nerve comparison groupoid} has these presentations as
objects and finite zigzags of elementary comparisons and formal inverses as
morphisms, with composition given by concatenation of zigzags. We say that two
presentations are comparison-equivalent when they lie in the same connected
component of this groupoid. Thus the comparison data carried by a finite
zigzag are part of the pseudofunctorial assignment; no path independence
between distinct zigzags is asserted unless an additional coherence
hypothesis is imposed.
\end{definition}

### sec_homological_visibility_intrinsic.tex
\begin{definition}[Finite-nerve-class visible quotient]\label{def:intrinsic-visible-quotient}
In the setting of \Cref{def:finite-nerve-presentation}, define the \emph{finite-nerve-class hidden subgroup}
\[
K_{\omega}:=\mathrm{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_{\omega})
\]
and the associated \emph{finite-nerve-class visible quotient}
\[
A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\omega}:=\operatorname{coker}(\mathrm{ev}_{\omega})=A/K_{\omega}.
\]
These terms are relative to the finite nerve comparison groupoid of
\Cref{def:finite-nerve-comparison-relation}; no presentation-free quotient is
asserted outside that groupoid.
\end{definition}

### sec_homological_visibility_intrinsic.tex
\begin{definition}[Class-admissible characters]\label{def:class-admissible-character}
In the setting of \Cref{def:finite-nerve-presentation}, let
\[
X_{\omega}:=\{\chi\in\widehat A\mid \chi_*(\omega)=0\},
\qquad
\widehat A:=\mathrm{Hom}(A,\mathbb T).
\]
Elements of $X_{\omega}$ are called \emph{class-admissible} for $\omega$.
\end{definition}

### sec_homological_visibility_intrinsic.tex
\begin{definition}[Chain-level evaluation of a presentation]\label{def:chain-level-evaluation}
Let $\alpha\in Z^2(N(\mathcal U),A)$ be a finite obstruction presentation of the class $\omega$. Write
\[
C_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)
\]
for the simplicial group of integral $2$-chains on the finite nerve. The \emph{chain-level evaluation map} of $\alpha$ is the homomorphism
\[
\widetilde\alpha:C_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)\to A
\]
defined by linear extension from the oriented $2$-simplices:
\[
\widetilde\alpha\!\left(\sum_{\sigma} n_{\sigma}\sigma\right)
:=
\sum_{\sigma} n_{\sigma}\alpha(\sigma).
\]
\end{definition}

### sec_homological_visibility_intrinsic.tex
\begin{definition}[Intrinsic strictification code]\label{def:intrinsic-strictification-code}
An \emph{intrinsic strictification code} for the obstruction class $\omega$ consists of a finite set $R$ and an injective map
\[
\iota_{\omega}:A\hookrightarrow A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\omega}\times R
\]
such that
\[
\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\iota_{\omega}=\pi_{\omega}.
\]
\end{definition}

### sec_information_states.tex
\begin{definition}[Information state]\label{def:information-state}
An \emph{information state} in $M$ is a pair
\[
p=(\Gamma_p,R_p)
\]
such that $\Gamma_p$ is a context and $\varnothing\neq R_p\subseteq \Val_M(\Gamma_p)$. The set of information states in $M$ is denoted by $\St(M)$.
\end{definition}

### sec_information_states.tex
\begin{definition}[Refinement]\label{def:refinement}
For states $p=(\Gamma_p,R_p)$ and $q=(\Gamma_q,R_q)$ in the same model, write $q\le p$ if
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item $\Gamma_p\preceq\Gamma_q$,
\item every $\sigma\in R_q$ satisfies $\sigma|_{\Gamma_p}\in R_p$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{definition}

### sec_information_states.tex
\begin{definition}[State forcing]\label{def:state-forcing}
Let $p=(\Gamma_p,R_p)\in\St(M)$ and let $\varphi$ be a formula well formed in context $\Gamma_p$. We define
\[
M,p\Vdash\varphi
\quad:\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\forall \rho\in R_p\;(M,\rho\models\varphi).
\]
\end{definition}

### sec_information_states.tex
\begin{definition}[State theory]\label{def:state-theory}
For $p\in\St(M)$, define
\[
\Th_M(p):=\{\varphi\mid M,p\Vdash\varphi\}.
\]
\end{definition}

### sec_information_states.tex
\begin{definition}[Decidedness]\label{def:decidedness}
A formula $\varphi$ is \emph{decided} at $p$, written $M,p\Downarrow\varphi$, if
\[
M,p\Vdash\varphi
\qquad\text{or}\qquad
M,p\Vdash\neg\varphi.
\]
\end{definition}

### sec_information_states.tex
\begin{definition}[State semantic consequence]\label{def:state-semantic-consequence}
For formulas $\Phi\cup\{\varphi\}$, define
\[
\Phi\models_{\mathrm{S}}\varphi
\]
to mean that for every model $M$ and every state $p\in\St(M)$,
\[
M,p\Vdash\Phi
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
M,p\Vdash\varphi.
\]
\end{definition}

### sec_null_decomposition.tex
\begin{definition}[Reference classes]\label{def:reference-classes}
For each state $p$ and each referenceable sort $s$, fix a set
\[
\mathcal R_s(p)
\]
and a surjective assignment
\[
r\longmapsto [r]_p\in \mathcal R_s(p)
\]
defined for the admitted references $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ at $p$. The element $[r]_p$ is called the \emph{reference class} of $r$ at $p$. The later local reference site is built on these classes; no further quotient structure is needed here.
\end{definition}

### sec_null_decomposition.tex
\begin{definition}[Local reference site]\label{def:local-reference-frame}
For a state $p$ and a referenceable sort $s$, a \emph{local reference site} consists of the following data.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item A reflexive, transitive refinement relation $\sqsubseteq_{p,s}$ on $\mathcal R_s(p)$.
\item The associated small thin category $\mathcal B_{p,s}$ whose objects are the elements of $\mathcal R_s(p)$ and in which there is a unique morphism
\[
b\longrightarrow a
\]
if and only if $b\sqsubseteq_{p,s} a$.
\item A Grothendieck pretopology $\Cov_{p,s}$ on $\mathcal B_{p,s}$ satisfying the identity, pullback-stability, and transitivity axioms.
\item The standing pullback hypothesis that, for every covering family
\[
\{a_i\to a\}_{i\in I}\in \Cov_{p,s}(a)
\]
and every pair $(i,j)$, the fibre product
\[
a_i\times_a a_j
\]
exists in $\mathcal B_{p,s}$.
\end{enumerate}
The fibre product clause is a condition on the site, not on a later
\v{C}ech cochain display: if two members of a covering family are
disjoint in a concrete presentation, their pullback must still be
represented by an object of the site, typically a strict initial object.
One may omit such empty pullback objects from a nonzero \v{C}ech nerve or
from a cochain complex whose coefficient sheaf has only the zero section
there, but not from the local reference site itself. Because
$\mathcal B_{p,s}$ is thin, the fibre product $a_i\times_a a_j$ is the
meet of $a_i$ and $a_j$ over $a$ whenever that meet exists. We write
\[
\mathcal C_{p,s}:=(\mathcal B_{p,s},\Cov_{p,s})
\]
for the resulting site.
\end{definition}

### sec_null_decomposition.tex
\begin{definition}[Local object functor]\label{def:local-object-functor}
A \emph{local object functor} on $(p,s)$ is a contravariant functor
\[
F_{p,s}:\mathcal{B}_{p,s}^{op}\to\mathsf{Set}.
\]
If $b\sqsubseteq_{p,s} a$, the induced restriction map is denoted by
\[
\res_b^a:F_{p,s}(a)\to F_{p,s}(b).
\]
\end{definition}

### sec_null_decomposition.tex
\begin{definition}[Three existence levels]\label{def:existence-levels}
Let $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ and assume $M,p\Vdash \Adm_s(r)$. Write $a=[r]_p$.
In the pullback-based local reference site of \Cref{def:local-reference-frame}, overlaps are checked on the fibre products $a_i\times_a a_j$ supplied there, rather than on semilattice meets.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item $M,p\Vdash \LocSec_s(r)$ if some cover $\mathcal U=\{a_i\to a\}_{i\in I}\in\Cov_{p,s}(a)$ has $F_{p,s}(a_i)\neq\varnothing$ for every $i\in I$.
\item $M,p\Vdash \CompSec_s(r)$ if some cover $\mathcal U=\{a_i\to a\}_{i\in I}\in\Cov_{p,s}(a)$ carries a matching family $(\sigma_i)_{i\in I}$ with each $\sigma_i\in F_{p,s}(a_i)$ and
\[
\res_{a_i\times_a a_j}^{a_i}(\sigma_i)=\res_{a_i\times_a a_j}^{a_j}(\sigma_j).
\]
\item $M,p\Vdash \Sec_s(r)$ if the fibre $F_{p,s}(a)$ is nonempty.
\end{enumerate}
\end{definition}

### sec_null_decomposition.tex
\begin{definition}[Separatedness at an object]\label{def:separated-at-a}
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site, let $F$ be a presheaf on $\mathcal C$, and let $a$ be an object of $\mathcal C$. We say that $F$ is \emph{separated at $a$} if for every covering family
\[
\{a_i\to a\}_{i\in I}
\]
and every pair of sections $\sigma,\tau\in F(a)$, the equalities
\[
\res_{a_i}^{a}(\sigma)=\res_{a_i}^{a}(\tau)
\qquad
(\forall i\in I)
\]
imply $\sigma=\tau$.
\end{definition}

### sec_null_decomposition.tex
\begin{definition}[Separatedness on the reference slice]\label{def:slice-separated-local-object}
For an admitted reference $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ at $p$, write
\[
a=[r]_p,
\qquad
\mathcal C_a:=\mathcal C_{p,s}/a.
\]
The restricted local-object presheaf $F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}$ is \emph{slice-separated} if it is separated at every object of $\mathcal C_a$.
Equivalently, separatedness is required not only at the terminal object
$a$, but also at every cover member, every pullback overlap, and every
object introduced by a refinement inside the slice. This distinction is
used essentially below: equality in a sheafification value over a cover
member gives equality of the original presheaf sections only after a
further cover of that cover member, and the upgrade back to equality over
the cover member itself requires separatedness at that object.
\end{definition}

### sec_null_decomposition.tex
\begin{definition}[Realization prestack and stackification]\label{def:realization-prestack}
Fix an admitted reference $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ at a state $p$, and write
\[
a=[r]_p,
\qquad
\mathcal C_a:=\mathcal C_{p,s}/a.
\]
A \emph{realization prestack} for $r$ at $p$ over the pullback-based slice site is a category fibred in groupoids
\[
\mathfrak P_r\to \mathcal C_a
\]
such that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item the pre-stackification connected-component presheaf is the restriction of the local object functor,
\[
\pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_r)\cong F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a};
\]
\item for every object $U$ of $\mathcal C_a$ and every $x\in \mathfrak P_r(U)$, the automorphism sheaf
\[
\underline{\mathrm{Aut}}(x)
\]
on $\mathcal C_a/U$ is functorially identified with the restriction of a fixed abelian sheaf $\Band$ on $\mathcal C_a$.
\end{enumerate}
Write
\[
\mathfrak L_r:=a(\mathfrak P_r)
\]
for the stackification of $\mathfrak P_r$ in groupoids \cite[Tag 02ZP]{StacksProject}.
\end{definition}

### sec_null_decomposition.tex
\begin{definition}[Global conservativity at the terminal fibre]\label{def:global-conservativity}
In the setting of \Cref{def:realization-prestack}, now over a pullback-based slice site $\mathcal C_a$, let
\[
\iota_r:\mathfrak P_r\to \mathfrak L_r:=a(\mathfrak P_r)
\]
be the stackification morphism. We say that $\mathfrak P_r$ is \emph{globally conservative at $a$} if every object of the terminal stack fibre $(\mathfrak L_r)_a$ is isomorphic to the image of some object of the terminal prestack fibre $(\mathfrak P_r)_a$; equivalently, the induced functor
\[
(\iota_r)_a:(\mathfrak P_r)_a\to (\mathfrak L_r)_a
\]
is essentially surjective.
\end{definition}

### sec_null_decomposition.tex
\begin{definition}[Terminal component effectivity]\label{def:terminal-component-effectivity}
In the setting of \Cref{def:realization-prestack}, the stackification
$\mathfrak L_r$ has \emph{effective terminal components} if the canonical
map from isomorphism classes of terminal-fibre objects to terminal sections
of the component sheaf,
\[
\pi_0\bigl(\mathfrak L_r(a)\bigr)\longrightarrow \pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a),
\]
is surjective. Equivalently, every section of the sheaf of connected
components over $a$ is represented by an actual object of
$\mathfrak L_r(a)$.
\end{definition}

### sec_null_decomposition.tex
\begin{definition}[Representative-rigid lift]\label{def:representative-rigid-lift}
In the setting of \Cref{def:realization-prestack} over the pullback-based slice site $\mathcal C_a$, a realization prestack
\[
\mathfrak P_r\to \mathcal C_a
\]
is called \emph{representative-rigid} if for every object $U$ of $\mathcal C_a$ there is a map
\[
s_U:F_{p,s}(U)\to \Ob(\mathfrak P_r(U))
\]
such that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item the image of $s_U(\sigma)$ in
\[
\pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_r)(U)\cong F_{p,s}(U)
\]
is $\sigma$;
\item for every morphism $f:V\to U$ in $\mathcal C_a$ and every $\sigma\in F_{p,s}(U)$,
\[
f^*s_U(\sigma)=s_V(\res_V^U(\sigma)).
\]
\end{enumerate}
Here \(f^*\) is computed with respect to a fixed split cleavage of the
fibred groupoid \(\mathfrak P_r\), so pullbacks compose on the nose. Thus
the isomorphism classes of local objects admit a strict functorial choice of
representatives. Without this split-cleavage convention the same condition
would have to be stated with coherent cartesian isomorphisms, and the proof
of descent below would require the corresponding triple-cocycle coherence
instead of literal equalities of pulled-back representatives.
\end{definition}

### sec_null_decomposition_part2.tex
\begin{definition}[Visible value classes]\label{def:visible-value-classes}
Let $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ be admitted at $p$, and write $a=[r]_p$. A \emph{visible presentation} of a value at $r$ is a local family of sections on some cover of $a$ in the pullback-based thin site of \Cref{def:local-reference-frame}; concretely, it is data
\[
\Bigl(\{a_i\to a\}_{i\in I},(\sigma_i)_{i\in I}\Bigr)
\]
with each $\sigma_i\in F_{p,s}(a_i)$ and with agreement after a covering
refinement of every pullback overlap $a_i\times_a a_j$. Two such
presentations are \emph{value-equivalent} when, after pulling both
families back to a common refinement of their covers and then to the
overlap refinements required by the plus construction, the resulting
local sections agree pointwise. A \emph{visible value class} is an
equivalence class under this refinement relation, and the set of all such
classes is denoted by $\Vis_{p,s}(r)$. If
$F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}$ is slice-separated, the local-overlap
refinements in this definition are unnecessary, so visible presentations
are the strict matching families of \Cref{def:existence-levels}(ii).
\end{definition}

### sec_null_decomposition_part2.tex
\begin{definition}[Typed readout]\label{def:typed-readout}
Let $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ and a state $p$ be given. Define the \emph{typed readout} of $r$ at $p$ by
\[
\Read_{p,s}(r):=
\begin{cases}
\Undef, & M,p\nVdash \Adm_s(r),\\[0.5ex]
v, & \Vis_{p,s}(r)=\{v\}\ \text{for some visible value class }v,\\[0.5ex]
\Null, & M,p\Vdash \Adm_s(r)\ \text{and}\ \Vis_{p,s}(r)\neq\{v\}\ \text{for every }v.
\end{cases}
\]
Thus a non-null readout occurs exactly when the admitted reference carries a unique visible value class.
\end{definition}

### sec_null_decomposition_part2.tex
\begin{definition}[Undefined, total, and null]\label{def:undef-total-null}
For an element $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ at a state $p$, define
\begin{align*}
M,p\Vdash \Undef_s(r)
&\quad:\Longleftrightarrow\quad
M,p\nVdash \Adm_s(r),\\
M,p\Vdash \Tot_s(r)
&\quad:\Longleftrightarrow\quad
M,p\Vdash \Adm_s(r)\land \Sec_s(r),\\
M,p\Vdash \Null_s(r)
&\quad:\Longleftrightarrow\quad
M,p\Vdash \Adm_s(r)\land \neg\Sec_s(r).
\end{align*}
Thus admitted references are partitioned into the total and null cases according to whether a global section exists, while non-admitted references are undefined.
\end{definition}

### sec_null_decomposition_part2.tex
\begin{definition}[The three null modes]\label{def:null-failure-modes}
For an admitted reference $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ at a state $p$, define
\begin{align*}
\Null_s^{\mathrm{loc}}(r)
&\quad:\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\Adm_s(r)\land \neg\LocSec_s(r),\\
\Null_s^{\mathrm{cmp}}(r)
&\quad:\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\Adm_s(r)\land \LocSec_s(r)\land \neg\CompSec_s(r),\\
\Null_s^{\mathrm{glue}}(r)
&\quad:\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\Adm_s(r)\land \CompSec_s(r)\land \neg\Sec_s(r).
\end{align*}
They record, respectively, failure already at the level of local sections, failure at compatibility, and failure only at the final gluing step.
\end{definition}

### sec_null_decomposition_part2.tex
\begin{definition}[Decomposition decidability]\label{def:decomposition-decidability}
Let $p$ be a state and $s\in S_{\mathrm{ref}}$. The local-object decomposition is said to be \emph{decided at $p$ for the sort $s$} if, for every admitted reference
\[
r:\mathsf{Ref}_s
\]
at $p$, both predicates
\[
\LocSec_s(r)
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\CompSec_s(r)
\]
are decided at $p$ in the sense of \Cref{def:decidedness}.
\end{definition}

### sec_null_decomposition_part2.tex
\begin{definition}[Automorphism-invariant lower comparison class]\label{def:lower-comparison-class}
Let $s\in S_{\mathrm{ref}}$. The automorphism-invariant lower comparison class $\mathcal{C}_{s}^{\mathrm{inv}}$ consists of the constant-free $\Sigma_1$-formulas with exactly one free variable of sort $\mathsf{Ref}_s$, no parameters of that sort, and any number of bound variables from the ambient pointwise signature. A formula $\varphi(x)\in\mathcal{C}_{s}^{\mathrm{inv}}$ is evaluated inside the constant-free $\Sigma_1$-reduct of an $\mathbb L_1$-model, and it is required to be invariant under automorphisms of that reduct.
\end{definition}

### sec_null_decomposition_part2.tex
\begin{definition}[Gluing-sensitive realization datum]\label{def:gluing-sensitive-realization}
Fix an admitted reference $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ at $p$ and write $a=[r]_p$. A \emph{gluing-sensitive realization datum} for $r$ is a tuple
\[
(\mathfrak P_r,\mathfrak L_r,\Band,\Cov_r^{\mathrm{acyc}})
\]
with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item $\mathfrak P_r\to\mathcal C_{p,s}/a$ is a realization prestack with band $\Band$ in the sense of \Cref{def:realization-prestack};
\item $\mathfrak L_r$ is a $\Band$-banded stack whose connected components agree with the sheafification of $F_{p,s}$, i.e.
\[
\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)\cong a_{p,s}F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_{p,s}/a};
\]
\item the stackification morphism $\iota_r:\mathfrak P_r\to\mathfrak L_r$ is globally conservative at $a$ in the sense of \Cref{def:global-conservativity};
\item for each visible branch supported by the datum, the induced family
\(\Cov_v^{\mathrm{acyc}}(a)\) is part of a \v{C}ech--derived comparison
package in the sense of \Cref{def:cech-derived-comparison-package}; in
particular, its covers admit \v{C}ech nerves in the slice, trivialize the
band where the obstruction cocycles are computed, and carry the specified
comparison isomorphism to derived cohomology.
\end{enumerate}
If such a datum exists we say that $r$ admits a gluing-sensitive realization. This datum is extra structure on top of the bare local object functor: later sections treat the gerbe-theoretic layer only relative to a chosen datum of this kind and do not assert that every local object functor admits one.
\end{definition}

### sec_preliminaries.tex
\begin{definition}[Logic layer]\label{def:logic-layer}
A \emph{logic layer} is a tuple
\[
\mathbb{L}=(\Sigma,\mathrm{Form},\Mod,\St,\Vdash,\models),
\]
where $\Sigma$ is a signature, $\mathrm{Form}$ is the class of well-formed $\Sigma$-formulas, $\Mod$ is a class of admissible models, $\St$ assigns to every $M\in\Mod$ a nonempty set $\St(M)$ of states, $\Vdash$ is a forcing relation on model-state pairs, and $\models$ is the induced consequence relation defined by
\[
\Gamma\models\varphi
\quad:\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\forall M\in\Mod\;\forall p\in\St(M)\,
\bigl(M,p\Vdash\Gamma \Rightarrow M,p\Vdash\varphi\bigr).
\]
\end{definition}

### sec_preliminaries.tex
\begin{definition}[Conservative extension]\label{def:conservative-extension}
Let
\[
\mathbb{L}_m=(\Sigma_m,\mathrm{Form}_m,\Mod_m,\St_m,\Vdash_m,\models_m)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\mathbb{L}_n=(\Sigma_n,\mathrm{Form}_n,\Mod_n,\St_n,\Vdash_n,\models_n)
\]
with $m<n$. We say that $\mathbb{L}_n$ is a \emph{conservative extension} of $\mathbb{L}_m$, written $\mathbb{L}_m\preceq\mathbb{L}_n$, if there exist
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item a language embedding $e_{m,n}:\Sigma_m\hookrightarrow\Sigma_n$,
\item a forgetful functor $U_{n,m}:\Mod_n\to\Mod_m$,
\item for every $M\in\Mod_n$, a state projection
\[
\pi^M_{n,m}:\St_n(M)\to \St_m\bigl(U_{n,m}(M)\bigr),
\]
\end{enumerate}
such that for every $\varphi\in \mathrm{Form}_m$, every $M\in\Mod_n$, and every $p\in\St_n(M)$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:conservative-extension}
M,p\Vdash_n \varphi
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
U_{n,m}(M),\pi^M_{n,m}(p)\Vdash_m \varphi.
\end{equation}
\end{definition}

### sec_preliminaries.tex
\begin{definition}[Singleton semantic embedding]\label{def:singleton-semantic-embedding}
Let $\mathbb{L}_0=(\Sigma_0,\mathrm{Form}_0,\Mod_0,\St_0,\Vdash_0,\models_0)$ and $\mathbb{L}_1=(\Sigma_1,\mathrm{Form}_1,\Mod_1,\St_1,\Vdash_1,\models_1)$. We say that $\mathbb{L}_0$ \emph{embeds into $\mathbb{L}_1$ by a singleton semantic embedding}, written $\mathbb{L}_0\hookrightarrow\mathbb{L}_1$, if there exist
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item a language embedding $e_{0,1}:\Sigma_0\hookrightarrow\Sigma_1$,
\item a forgetful functor $U_{1,0}:\Mod_1\to\Mod_0$,
\item for every $M\in\Mod_1$ and every pointwise state $\rho\in\St_0(U_{1,0}(M))$, a canonical singleton state
\[
\iota_{0,1}^M(\rho)\in\St_1(M)
\]
\end{enumerate}
such that for every $\varphi\in\mathrm{Form}_0$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:singleton-semantic-embedding}
M,\iota_{0,1}^M(\rho)\Vdash_1\varphi
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
U_{1,0}(M),\rho\Vdash_0\varphi.
\end{equation}
\end{definition}

sec_introduction.tex:14:The second part begins once the set-valued local-object functor is enriched by groupoid-valued data. \Cref{thm:canonical-lift-rigidity} gives a rigidity statement for representative-rigid lifts: if the local-object presheaf is slice-separated and a realization prestack admits a strict functorial choice of representatives and is globally conservative at the terminal fibre, then the sheafification unit is surjective there; under $H^1$-vanishing and the same slice-separatedness, this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf at the terminal fibre. Thus gluing-level nullity is necessarily tied to genuinely gluing-sensitive lift data. \Cref{thm:intrinsic-branch-obstruction-extension} identifies the canonicity that survives at this level: once the sheafified local object functor has been lifted to a banded realization stack, the branch obstruction map to derived $H^2$ is intrinsic up to equivalence of banded extensions. For such an extension, visible value classes are the global sections of the sheaf of connected components (\Cref{thm:visible-value-components}), each visible branch determines a banded component gerbe (\Cref{thm:component-gerbe-decomposition}), and, on slice-separated reference slices, \Cref{thm:gerbe-null-semantics} identifies gluing-level absence with the existence of visible branches together with non-neutrality of the corresponding component gerbes. No general existence theorem for gluing-sensitive lifts is proved; Appendix~\ref{sec:appendix-ghz} gives an explicit GHZ/Mermin example of chosen lift data.

\section{Comparison of branches and realization}\label{sec:branch-aggregation}

We compare the quotients attached to the different visible branches of a single admitted reference. Retaining the branch label leads to a branch-sensitive quotient, while forgetting it leads to a branch-uniform quotient. The comparison results below are formal once the branchwise intrinsic data have been fixed, whereas the realization theorems later in the section remain internal to explicitly chosen finite nerves and constant bands.

\begin{definition}[Branchwise intrinsic data]\label{def:branchwise-intrinsic-data}
Fix an admitted reference $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ at a state $p$, and assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item the hypotheses of \Cref{def:cech-gluing-obstruction} hold;
\item the set $\Vis_{p,s}(r)$ is finite and nonempty;
\item every component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ is banded by the same finite abelian group $A$ and admits a finite nerve presentation of its branch obstruction class $\omega_v$.
\end{enumerate}
For each visible branch $v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)$, write
\[
K_v:=K_{\omega_v},
\qquad
A_{\mathrm{vis}}^v:=A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\omega_v}=A/K_v,
\qquad
\pi_v:A\twoheadrightarrow A_{\mathrm{vis}}^v.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Branch-sensitive visible quotient]\label{thm:branch-sensitive-visible-quotient}
In the setting of \Cref{def:branchwise-intrinsic-data}, consider the diagonal map
\[
\Delta_{\mathrm{br}}:A\longrightarrow \prod_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} A_{\mathrm{vis}}^v,
\qquad
x\longmapsto (\pi_v(x))_v.
\]
Then
\[
\ker(\Delta_{\mathrm{br}})=\bigcap_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v.
\]
Consequently, the quotient
\[
A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{br}}(r):=A\Big/\bigcap_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v
\]
is canonically isomorphic to $\mathrm{Im}(\Delta_{\mathrm{br}})$. It is the maximal quotient of $A$ that remains visible once the branch label itself is allowed as part of the semantic context.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For $x\in A$ one has $\Delta_{\mathrm{br}}(x)=0$ if and only if $\pi_v(x)=0$ for every visible branch $v$, which is equivalent to $x\in K_v$ for every $v$. Hence
\[
\ker(\Delta_{\mathrm{br}})=\bigcap_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v.
\]
The first isomorphism theorem therefore yields
\[
\mathrm{Im}(\Delta_{\mathrm{br}})
\cong
A\Big/\bigcap_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v.
\]
Thus, once the visible branch is known, two elements of $A$ remain semantically indistinguishable exactly when they are indistinguishable on every individual branch quotient.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Branch-uniform visible quotient]\label{thm:branch-uniform-visible-quotient}
In the setting of \Cref{def:branchwise-intrinsic-data}, let
\[
X_v:=\{\chi\in \widehat A\mid \chi_*(\omega_v)=0\}
\]
for each visible branch $v$, and define the uniformly admissible characters by
\[
X^{\mathrm{unif}}(r):=\bigcap_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} X_v.
\]
Then
\[
X^{\mathrm{unif}}(r)=\mathrm{Ann}\Bigl(\sum_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v\Bigr).
\]
Consequently, the quotient
\[
A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{unif}}(r):=A\Big/\sum_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v
\]
is exactly the quotient detected by the characters that are admissible on every visible branch simultaneously.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{thm:intrinsic-visible-quotient}, one has
\[
X_v=\mathrm{Ann}(K_v)
\]
for every $v$. Therefore
\[
X^{\mathrm{unif}}(r)
=
\bigcap_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} \mathrm{Ann}(K_v)
=
\mathrm{Ann}\Bigl(\sum_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v\Bigr),
\]
where the last identity is the standard annihilator formula for finite abelian groups \cite[Part~I, Chap.~2]{Terras1999}. Finite abelian duality then gives
\[
\bigcap_{\chi\in X^{\mathrm{unif}}(r)} \ker\chi
=
\sum_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v.
\]
Hence the quotient detected by all uniformly admissible characters is precisely
\[
A\Big/\sum_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v.
\qedhere
\]
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Branch comparison map and resolution kernel]\label{def:branch-comparison-map}
In the setting of \Cref{def:branchwise-intrinsic-data}, let
\[
\pi_{\mathrm{br}}:A\twoheadrightarrow A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{br}}(r)
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\pi_{\mathrm{unif}}:A\twoheadrightarrow A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{unif}}(r)
\]
be the canonical quotient maps. Since
\[
\bigcap_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v
\subseteq
\sum_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v,
\]
there is a unique surjective homomorphism
\[
\beta_r:A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{br}}(r)\twoheadrightarrow A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{unif}}(r)
\]
such that
\[
\beta_r\circ \pi_{\mathrm{br}}=\pi_{\mathrm{unif}}.
\]
Its kernel is denoted
\[
B_{\mathrm{res}}(r):=
\ker(\beta_r)
\cong
\Bigl(\sum_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v\Bigr)\Big/\Bigl(\bigcap_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v\Bigr)
\]
and called the \emph{branch-resolution kernel}.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact comparison of branch-sensitive and branch-uniform visibility]\label{thm:branch-comparison-exact-sequence}
In the setting of \Cref{def:branch-comparison-map}, there is a short exact sequence
\[
0\longrightarrow B_{\mathrm{res}}(r)\longrightarrow A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{br}}(r)\xrightarrow{\ \beta_r\ } A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{unif}}(r)\longrightarrow 0.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\ker(\beta_r)
\cong
\Bigl(\sum_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v\Bigr)\Big/\Bigl(\bigcap_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v\Bigr).
\]
Thus the precise gap between branch-sensitive and branch-uniform visibility is measured by the lattice interval from $\bigcap_v K_v$ to $\sum_v K_v$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Existence and uniqueness of $\beta_r$ follow from the universal property of the quotient because
\[
\bigcap_v K_v\subseteq \sum_v K_v.
\]
Surjectivity is immediate from surjectivity of $\pi_{\mathrm{unif}}$. By the third isomorphism theorem,
\[
\ker(\beta_r)
\cong
\Bigl(\sum_v K_v\Bigr)\Big/\Bigl(\bigcap_v K_v\Bigr),
\]
which gives the claimed exact sequence.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Criterion for the absence of branch gain]\label{cor:no-branch-gain-criterion}
In the setting of \Cref{def:branch-comparison-map}, the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item $\beta_r$ is an isomorphism;
\item $B_{\mathrm{res}}(r)=0$;
\item
\[
\bigcap_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v
=
\sum_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v;
\]
\item the hidden subgroups are branch-constant:
\[
K_v=K_w
\qquad
(\forall v,w\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)).
\]
\end{enumerate}
Hence branch sensitivity yields no additional visible information exactly when all visible branches have the same finite-nerve-class hidden subgroup.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The equivalence of \textup{(i)} and \textup{(ii)} is exactness of the sequence in \Cref{thm:branch-comparison-exact-sequence}. Condition \textup{(ii)} is equivalent to \textup{(iii)} by the quotient description of $B_{\mathrm{res}}(r)$.

 succeeded in 691ms:
\begin{proof}
By \Cref{thm:intrinsic-visible-quotient},
\[
X_{\omega}=\mathrm{Ann}(K_{\omega})=K_{\omega}^{\perp}.
\]
Characters of $A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\omega}=A/K_{\omega}$ are exactly the characters of $A$ that kill $K_{\omega}$, so precomposition with $\pi_{\omega}$ identifies $\widehat{A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\omega}}$ with $X_{\omega}$. The separation statement follows from finite abelian duality applied to the finite group $A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\omega}$ \cite[Part~I, Chap.~2]{Terras1999}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Initiality among pure-extension quotients]\label{thm:intrinsic-pure-ext-initiality}
In the finite nerve presentation of \Cref{def:finite-nerve-presentation}, let
\[
\pi_\omega:A\twoheadrightarrow A_{\mathrm{vis}}^\omega=A/K_\omega
\]
be the finite-nerve-class visible quotient. For every surjective homomorphism $q:A\twoheadrightarrow B$, the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item $q$ factors uniquely through $\pi_\omega$;
\item $q$ kills $\operatorname{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_\omega)=K_\omega$;
\item $\eta_B(q_*\omega)=0$;
\item $q_*(\omega)$ lies in the pure $\operatorname{Ext}$ subgroup
\[
\operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),B)
\subseteq H^2(N(\mathcal U),B)
\]
of the universal coefficient sequence.
\end{enumerate}
Thus $A_{\mathrm{vis}}^\omega$ is initial among coefficient quotients for which the pushed-forward obstruction has no $H_2$-visible part. This is the pullback-site, finite-nerve form of the companion initiality theorem \cite[Theorem~6.13]{MaZhang2026ConditionalGluingFailure}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The equivalence of \textup{(i)} and \textup{(ii)} is the universal property of the quotient
\[
\pi_\omega:A\twoheadrightarrow A/K_\omega.
\]
Indeed, a homomorphism $q:A\to B$ factors uniquely through $\pi_\omega$ if and only if $K_\omega\subseteq\ker q$, which is exactly the assertion that $q$ kills $\operatorname{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_\omega)$.

For \textup{(ii)} and \textup{(iii)}, use naturality of the universal coefficient map with respect to the coefficient homomorphism $q$. The naturality square gives
\[
\eta_B(q_*\omega)=q\circ \eta_A(\omega)=q\circ \mathrm{ev}_\omega.
\]
Thus $\eta_B(q_*\omega)=0$ if and only if $q$ vanishes on the image of $\mathrm{ev}_\omega$, namely on $K_\omega$.

Finally, the universal coefficient exact sequence for the finite nerve is
\[
0\to \operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),B)
\to H^2(N(\mathcal U),B)
\xrightarrow{\eta_B}
\operatorname{Hom}(H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),B)
\to 0.
\]
Therefore $\eta_B(q_*\omega)=0$ if and only if $q_*(\omega)$ lies in the kernel of $\eta_B$, which is precisely the displayed pure $\operatorname{Ext}$ subgroup. This proves all equivalences and the initiality statement.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Class-trivializing initiality when $H_1$ vanishes]\label{cor:h1-vanishing-class-trivializing}
Assume
\[
H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)=0.
\]
Then, for every surjective homomorphism $q:A\twoheadrightarrow B$, the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item $q_*(\omega)=0$ in $H^2(N(\mathcal U),B)$;
\item $q$ factors uniquely through
\[
\pi_{\omega}:A\twoheadrightarrow A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\omega}.
\]
\end{enumerate}
Hence, when $H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)=0$, the finite-nerve-class visible quotient is initial among coefficient quotients that annihilate the obstruction class itself.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
If $H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)=0$, then
\[
\operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),B)=0
\]
for every abelian group $B$. Thus, in the criterion of \Cref{thm:intrinsic-pure-ext-initiality}, the pure-extension condition is equivalent to $q_*(\omega)=0$, and the conclusion follows.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Presentation-object visibility without a canonical splitting]\label{rem:no-canonical-splitting}
A/H_\alpha
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\omega}=A/K_{\omega}.
\]
The equivalence of \textup{(ii)} and \textup{(iii)} is exactly \Cref{prop:chain-vs-homological-visibility}(iii).
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Character-blind pure-extension obstructions]\label{thm:character-blind-obstructions}
In the setting of \Cref{def:finite-nerve-presentation}, with a chosen admitted
reference, visible branch, realization prestack, trivialized constant finite
abelian band $A$, and the \textup{(H4)} comparison datum needed to regard
$\omega$ as a derived branch class, the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item $K_{\omega}=0$;
\item $A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\omega}=A$;
\item $\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=0$;
\item $\omega$ lies in the subgroup
\[
\operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),A)\subseteq H^2(N(\mathcal U),A).
\]
\end{enumerate}
If these conditions hold and $\omega\neq 0$, then the chosen branch gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ is non-neutral, while every character of $A$ is class-admissible for that branch. If, in addition, the realization prestack is globally conservative at the terminal fibre, \(F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}\) is slice-separated, and $|\Vis_{p,s}(r)|=1$, then
\[
M,p\Vdash \Null^{\mathrm{glue}}_s(r).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{def:intrinsic-visible-quotient},
\[
K_{\omega}=\mathrm{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}),
\]
so \textup{(i)} and \textup{(iii)} are equivalent. Since $A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\omega}=A/K_{\omega}$, conditions \textup{(i)} and \textup{(ii)} are equivalent. By the universal coefficient sequence, \textup{(iii)} holds exactly when $\omega\in\ker(\eta_A)$, and this kernel is the stated $\operatorname{Ext}$-subgroup. Hence all four conditions are equivalent.

If they hold and $\omega\neq 0$, then \Cref{prop:derived-branch-classification} shows that the branch gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ is non-neutral.
On the other hand, $\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=0$ implies
\[
\chi\circ \mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=0
\]
for every $\chi\in\widehat A$, so \Cref{thm:intrinsic-visible-quotient} shows that every character is class-admissible.

Assume now that \(F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}\) is slice-separated and that $|\Vis_{p,s}(r)|=1$. Since the chosen branch $v$ exists, \Cref{prop:compsecs-vs-visible-branches} gives
\[
M,p\Vdash \CompSec_s(r).
\]
Suppose towards a contradiction that
\[
M,p\Vdash \Sec_s(r).
\]
By \Cref{def:realization-prestack}(i), this yields an object of the terminal fibre $(\mathfrak P_r)_a$, and its image under the stackification morphism
\[
\iota_r:\mathfrak P_r\to \mathfrak L_r
\]
defines an object of $\mathfrak L_r(a)$. Because there is only one visible branch, every object of $\mathfrak L_r(a)$ lies in the unique component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v(a)$. Hence
\[
\mathfrak G_v(a)\neq\varnothing.
\]
By \Cref{lem:terminal-fibre-neutrality}, this implies that $\mathfrak G_v$ is neutral, contradicting the non-neutrality already proved. Therefore
\[
M,p\nVdash \Sec_s(r).
\]
Combining this with $M,p\Vdash \CompSec_s(r)$ and admittedness of $r$, we obtain
\[
M,p\Vdash \Null^{\mathrm{glue}}_s(r).
\]
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Automatic blindness when $H_2$ vanishes]\label{cor:h2-vanishing-blindness}
\[
(\mathcal C_a,\mathfrak P_r,A,\omega,\mathrm{ev}_\omega,K_\omega,A_{\mathrm{vis}}^\omega)
\]
inside a concrete site-theoretic example, once the realization stack has been fixed by the chosen cocycle data. It is the opposite extreme from the $\mathbb{R}P^2$ blind case of \Cref{ex:rp2-character-blind}: for an $\mathbb{R}P^2$-type nerve one has $K_\omega=0$, every character is class-admissible, and the obstruction is purely $\operatorname{Ext}$-type with $A_{\mathrm{vis}}^\omega=A$; for the present $S^2$-type nerve one has $K_\omega=A$, only the trivial character is class-admissible, and the obstruction is purely $H_2$-type with $A_{\mathrm{vis}}^\omega=0$.
\end{example}

\begin{definition}[Intrinsic strictification code]\label{def:intrinsic-strictification-code}
An \emph{intrinsic strictification code} for the obstruction class $\omega$ consists of a finite set $R$ and an injective map
\[
\iota_{\omega}:A\hookrightarrow A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\omega}\times R
\]
such that
\[
\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\iota_{\omega}=\pi_{\omega}.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Intrinsic hidden-state lower bound]\label{cor:intrinsic-hidden-state-lower-bound}
Every intrinsic strictification code satisfies
\[
|R|\ge |K_{\omega}|.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\log_2|R|\ge \log_2|K_{\omega}|.
\]
This lower bound is sharp.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{def:intrinsic-visible-quotient}, the fibers of $\pi_{\omega}$ are exactly the cosets of $K_{\omega}$, so every fiber has cardinality $|K_{\omega}|$. The same fiber-counting argument as in \Cref{thm:minimal-information-cost-of-strictification} therefore shows that any injective code preserving the first projection must satisfy $|R|\ge |K_{\omega}|$.

For sharpness, take $R:=K_{\omega}$ and choose a set-theoretic section $s_{\omega}:A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\omega}\to A$ of $\pi_{\omega}$. Then
\[
\iota_{\omega}(x):=\bigl(\pi_{\omega}(x),x-s_{\omega}(\pi_{\omega}(x))\bigr)
\]
is injective.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Prime decomposition of intrinsic visibility and budget]\label{thm:intrinsic-prime-decomposition}
Write the finite abelian group $A$ as a direct sum of its $p$-primary components:
\[
A=\bigoplus_p A_{(p)}.
\]
Let $\omega_p\in H^2(N(\mathcal U),A_{(p)})$ be the image of $\omega$ under the projection onto the $p$-primary summand. Then
\[
\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=\bigoplus_p \mathrm{ev}_{\omega_p},
\qquad
K_{\omega}=\bigoplus_p K_{\omega,p},
\qquad
A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\omega}\cong \bigoplus_p A_{(p)}/K_{\omega,p},
\]
where
\[
K_{\omega,p}:=\mathrm{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_{\omega_p}).
\]
Consequently,
\[
|K_{\omega}|=\prod_p |K_{\omega,p}|,
\qquad
\log_2|K_{\omega}|=\sum_p \log_2|K_{\omega,p}|.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Both $H^2(N(\mathcal U),-)$ and $\mathrm{Hom}(H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),-)$ commute with finite direct sums, so the universal coefficient map is compatible with the primary decomposition of $A$. Hence
\[
\eta_A(\omega)=\bigoplus_p \eta_{A_{(p)}}(\omega_p),
\]
which is exactly the asserted decomposition of $\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}$.

Taking images gives
\[
K_{\omega}
=
\mathrm{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_{\omega})
=
\bigoplus_p \mathrm{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_{\omega_p})
=
\bigoplus_p K_{\omega,p},
\]
by \Cref{def:intrinsic-visible-quotient}. The quotient decomposition follows immediately:
\[
A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\omega}
=
A/K_{\omega}
\cong
\bigoplus_p A_{(p)}/K_{\omega,p}.
\]
Since finite direct sums correspond to products of cardinalities, the budget formula is immediate.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Intrinsic budget versus strict budget]\label{cor:strict-intrinsic-budget-comparison}
For every finite obstruction presentation $\alpha$ of the class $\omega$,
\[
|K_{\omega}|\le |H_\alpha|,
\qquad
\log_2|K_{\omega}|\le \log_2|H_\alpha|.
\]
Hence the finite-nerve-class hidden-state budget never exceeds the strict presentation-level budget. Equality holds if and only if the canonical surjection
\[
A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\omega}\twoheadrightarrow A/H_\alpha
\]
is an isomorphism.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{cor:strict-to-intrinsic-visible}, there is a surjective homomorphism
\[
A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\omega}=A/K_{\omega}\twoheadrightarrow A/H_\alpha.
\]
For finite groups this implies
\[
|A|/|K_{\omega}|\ge |A|/|H_\alpha|,
\]
hence $|K_{\omega}|\le |H_\alpha|$. The logarithmic inequality is immediate. Equality of cardinalities holds exactly when the displayed surjection is bijective.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Maximal collapse criterion]\label{cor:maximal-collapse}
In the setting of \Cref{def:finite-nerve-presentation}, the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item $\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}:H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)\to A$ is surjective;
\item $K_{\omega}=A$;
\item $A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\omega}=0$;
\item the intrinsic strictification budget is maximal:
\[
\log_2|K_{\omega}|=\log_2|A|.
\]
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{def:intrinsic-visible-quotient}, $K_{\omega}=\mathrm{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_{\omega})$, so \textup{(i)} and \textup{(ii)} are equivalent. Condition \textup{(ii)} is equivalent to \textup{(iii)} by the definition of $A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\omega}=A/K_{\omega}$. For finite groups, \textup{(ii)} is also equivalent to $|K_{\omega}|=|A|$, which is exactly \textup{(iv)} after taking $\log_2$.
\end{proof}

 succeeded in 468ms:
The preceding corollary classifies the branchwise hidden subgroups that can occur on a fixed finite nerve with $H_2\cong \mathbb Z^\beta$. The next theorem replaces that abstract nerve by an explicitly chosen bouquet good-cover family and classifies, inside that family and with the stated realization data, the finite abelian groups that occur as pure two-branch resolution kernels.

All realization data in this subsection are chosen data: a finite simplicial
model $K_\beta$, the open-star good-cover system, a trivialization of the
constant finite abelian band, and the branch cocycles or homomorphisms used in
\Cref{thm:mixed-branch-realization}. The theorem below is not a canonical
classification over all presentations of the bouquet.

\begin{lemma}[Bouquet good-cover and finite-abelian interfaces]\label{lem:bouquet-cover-classical-interface}
Let $K$ be a finite simplicial complex and let $\mathcal U^{(m)}$ be the open-star cover of $\operatorname{Sd}^m K$ on $|K|$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item every nonempty finite intersection of members of $\mathcal U^{(m)}$ is contractible, and $N(\mathcal U^{(m)})$ is canonically isomorphic to $\operatorname{Sd}^mK$;
\item the covers $\mathcal U^{(m+1)}$ refine $\mathcal U^{(m)}$, and in the pullback site generated by all such open stars, their nonempty intersections, and a strict initial object for empty intersections, the family $(\mathcal U^{(m)})_{m\ge0}$ is filtered and cofinal;
\item for every constant finite abelian group $G$, the Leray--\v{C}ech comparison identifies
\[
\varinjlim_m\check H^2(\mathcal U^{(m)},G)
\cong
H^2(|K|,G),
\]
and the comparison is compatible with the simplicial cohomology of the nerves;
\item for every integer $\beta\ge 1$ and every nonzero finite abelian group $G$, the
group $G$ admits a decomposition
\[
G=G_1\oplus G_2
\]
with $G_1,G_2$ nonzero and $d(G_i)\le\beta$ for $i=1,2$ if and only if $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
For \textup{(i)}, the open star of a vertex of a barycentric subdivision is contractible, and a nonempty finite intersection of such open stars is the open star of the simplex spanned by the corresponding vertices. This is contractible. The nerve of the open-star cover of a barycentric subdivision is the subdivision itself; this is the standard nerve computation for open stars in a simplicial complex \cite[Secs.~2.1, 4G]{Hatcher2002}.

For \textup{(ii)}, barycentric subdivision gives a simplicial refinement of the previous subdivision, and each open star in $\operatorname{Sd}^{m+1}K$ lies in an open star of $\operatorname{Sd}^{m}K$. The generated site used here includes a strict initial object $\emptyset$ and declares the pullback of two disjoint members to be $\emptyset$; nonempty pullbacks are the corresponding finite intersections. Thus every pullback demanded by the local-reference-site axioms is represented in the site, while the \v{C}ech cochains still ignore empty intersections because the constant sheaf has only the zero section on $\emptyset$. The pretopology is generated by these covers, their pullbacks, identity covers, and the empty cover of $\emptyset$, so any covering family in the generated site is refined by a common later barycentric open-star cover. This proves filteredness and cofinality.

For \textup{(iii)}, the contractibility in \textup{(i)} makes each $\mathcal U^{(m)}$ a Leray cover for the genuine constant sheaf $G$ on the associated formal \v{C}ech site. Empty pullback objects contribute no cochains. The Leray theorem for \v{C}ech cohomology therefore identifies the \v{C}ech cohomology of these covers with the sheaf cohomology of $|K|$, and the nerve identification in \textup{(i)} identifies the same groups with simplicial cohomology of $\operatorname{Sd}^mK$ \cite[Chap.~III, Sec.~4]{Bredon1997}, \cite[Sec.~4G]{Hatcher2002}. The refinement maps are the usual subdivision maps, hence induce cohomology isomorphisms.

For \textup{(iv)}, fix an integer $\beta\ge1$. The standing nonzero hypothesis removes the trivial group from the classification; here a cyclic $p$-group means a cyclic group of order $p^n$ with $n\ge1$. First suppose such a decomposition exists. Then $G$ is a direct sum of two nonzero groups, so it is decomposable. The finite abelian indecomposable groups are exactly the cyclic groups of prime-power order \cite[Chap.~12]{DummitFoote2004}. Also
\[
d(G)\le d(G_1)+d(G_2)\le 2\beta.
\]
Conversely, assume $d(G)\le2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group. There are two cases: either the minimal number of generators is $m\ge2$, or $m=1$ and the cyclic group has non-prime-power order. If $d(G)=m\ge2$, write an invariant-factor decomposition
\[
G\cong C_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus C_{n_m},
\qquad
n_1\mid n_2\mid\cdots\mid n_m.
\]
With $t=\min\{\beta,m-1\}$, the two sums
\[
G_1=C_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus C_{n_t},
\qquad
G_2=C_{n_{t+1}}\oplus\cdots\oplus C_{n_m}
\]
are nonzero and satisfy $d(G_1)\le\beta$ and $d(G_2)=m-t\le\beta$. If $d(G)=1$, then $G$ is cyclic. Since it is not a cyclic $p$-group, its order has at least two coprime factors $a,b>1$, and the Chinese remainder theorem gives
\[
G\cong \mathbb Z/a\mathbb Z\oplus\mathbb Z/b\mathbb Z,
\]
with both summands nonzero and singly generated. This proves the equivalence.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Bouquet mixed-realization transfer]\label{lem:bouquet-mixed-realization-transfer}
Fix $\beta\ge 1$ and the bouquet site $\mathcal C_a$ built from
$K_\beta$ and the open-star covers $\mathcal U_\beta^{(m)}$ as in
\Cref{thm:bouquet-two-branch-resolution}. Let $G$ be a finite abelian
group, and let $G_1,G_2\le G$ be nonzero subgroups satisfying
\[
d(G_i)\le \beta\qquad(i=1,2).
\]
Then there exist a state $p$, an admitted reference $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$
inside a model $M$ with $a=[r]_p$, a local object functor on
$\mathcal C_a$, and a realization prestack with constant band $G$ such
that
\[
\Vis_{p,s}(r)=\{v_1,v_2\},
\qquad
K_{v_i}=G_i\quad(i=1,2).
\]
Both component gerbes are non-neutral. If, moreover,
\[
G_1\cap G_2=0,\qquad G_1+G_2=G,
\]
then
\[
A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{br}}(r)\cong B_{\mathrm{res}}(r)\cong G,
\qquad
A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{unif}}(r)=0,
\qquad
M,p\Vdash \Null_s^{\mathrm{glue}}(r).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{lem:bouquet-cover-classical-interface}(i)--(iii), the cover
$\mathcal U_\beta^{(0)}$ is a finite good cover whose nerve is
$K_\beta$, all finite intersections are contractible, the constant band
$G$ is trivial on the cover, and the generated filtered family satisfies
\textup{(H4)}. Since $K_\beta\simeq\bigvee_{j=1}^{\beta}S^2$, we have
\[
H_1\bigl(N(\mathcal U_\beta^{(0)}),\mathbb Z\bigr)=0,
\qquad
H_2\bigl(N(\mathcal U_\beta^{(0)}),\mathbb Z\bigr)\cong \mathbb Z^\beta.
\]
The inequalities $d(G_i)\le\beta$ therefore allow homomorphisms
\[
\phi_i:H_2\bigl(N(\mathcal U_\beta^{(0)}),\mathbb Z\bigr)\to G
\]
with $\operatorname{Im}(\phi_i)=G_i$.

Apply \Cref{thm:mixed-branch-realization} to the fixed finite nerve,
constant band $A:=G$, branch index set $\{1,2\}$, and homomorphisms
$\phi_1,\phi_2$. It constructs the asserted one-state realization data
and gives
\[
K_{v_i}=\operatorname{Im}(\phi_i)=G_i.
\]
The model constructed here is therefore admissible for the same reason as in
\Cref{thm:mixed-branch-realization}: it is obtained by the layer-expansion
interface of \Cref{prop:admissible-layer-expansion-interface}.
Since $G_i\ne0$, the same theorem makes both component gerbes
non-neutral.

Under the additional direct-sum hypotheses, the branch-sensitive hidden
subgroup intersection is $0$ and the branch-uniform hidden subgroup sum
is all of $G$. The quotient formulas in
\Cref{thm:branch-sensitive-visible-quotient,thm:branch-uniform-visible-quotient,thm:branch-comparison-exact-sequence}
therefore give
\[
A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{br}}(r)\cong B_{\mathrm{res}}(r)\cong G,
\qquad
A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{unif}}(r)=0.
\]
Finally, because both branches are non-neutral,
\Cref{thm:mixed-branch-realization}(iv) gives
$M,p\Vdash \Null_s^{\mathrm{glue}}(r)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Admissible-expansion two-branch resolution on chosen bouquet good covers]\label{thm:bouquet-two-branch-resolution}
Fix an integer $\beta\ge 1$, let $K_\beta$ be a finite connected simplicial complex whose geometric realization is homotopy equivalent to
\[
\bigvee_{j=1}^{\beta} S^2,
\]
and write
\[
X_\beta:=|K_\beta|.
\]
For each $m\ge 0$, let
\[
\mathcal U_\beta^{(m)}
\]
be the open-star cover of the barycentric subdivision $\operatorname{Sd}^m K_\beta$, viewed as a cover of $X_\beta$. Let $\mathcal C_a$ be the pullback site whose objects are $X_\beta$, a strict initial object $\emptyset$, and all nonempty finite intersections of members of the covers $\mathcal U_\beta^{(m)}$; the pullback of two objects over a common target is their nonempty intersection when it is nonempty and is $\emptyset$ otherwise. Covering families are generated by the families $\mathcal U_\beta^{(m)}$, their pullbacks, identity covers, and the empty cover of $\emptyset$.
All admissible-expansion realization assertions in this theorem are understood relative to the
well-typed admissible-expansion convention of
\Cref{prop:admissible-layer-expansion-interface}.

Then the family
\[
\bigl(\mathcal U_\beta^{(m)}\bigr)_{m\ge 0}
\]
is a filtered cofinal family satisfying \textup{(H4)} for every constant finite abelian band.

Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, and write $d(G)$ for the minimal number of generators of $G$. Then the following are equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item $G\ne0$, $d(G)\le 2\beta$, and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, where
cyclic $p$-group means cyclic of order $p^n$ with $n\ge1$.
\item In the admissible-expansion model class generated by
\Cref{prop:admissible-layer-expansion-interface}, the one-state
\(\mathbb L_1\)-reduct, the site \(\mathcal C_a\), a local object functor on
\(\mathcal C_a\), and a realization prestack
\[
\mathfrak P_r\to \mathcal C_a
\]
with trivialized constant band $G$ define a one-state
\(\mathbb L_2/\mathbb L_3\) model \(M\) with state \(p\) and admitted
reference \(r:\mathsf{Ref}_s\), \(a=[r]_p\), using the finite-nerve Leray
comparison supplied by the chosen bouquet good covers, such that
\[
\Vis_{p,s}(r)=\{v_1,v_2\},
\]
both component gerbes $\mathfrak G_{v_1}$ and $\mathfrak G_{v_2}$ are non-neutral, and
\[
K_{v_1}\cap K_{v_2}=0,
\qquad
K_{v_1}+K_{v_2}=G.
\]
\end{enumerate}
Whenever these conditions hold,
\[
A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{br}}(r)\cong B_{\mathrm{res}}(r)\cong G,
\qquad
A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{unif}}(r)=0,
\qquad
M,p\Vdash \Null_s^{\mathrm{glue}}(r).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
We use four explicit interfaces: the good-cover comparison, the
finite-abelian decomposition, the mixed-realization transfer, and the
branch-exactness consequence.

The good-cover interface is supplied by
\Cref{lem:bouquet-cover-classical-interface}. By clause \textup{(i)},
each $\mathcal U_\beta^{(m)}$ is a finite good cover of $X_\beta$, its
nonempty finite intersections are contractible, and
\[
N(\mathcal U_\beta^{(m)})\cong \operatorname{Sd}^{m}K_\beta.
\]
Thus the constant band $G$ is trivial on every such cover, and
\[
H^1(U_{i_0\cdots i_n},G)=0
\]
for every nonempty intersection appearing in the \v{C}ech descent
argument. Clause \textup{(ii)} makes
$\bigl(\mathcal U_\beta^{(m)}\bigr)_{m\ge 0}$ filtered and cofinal in the
generated pretopology of $\mathcal C_a$, and clause \textup{(iii)}
identifies the filtered \v{C}ech system with derived cohomology. Hence
the family satisfies \textup{(H4)} for every constant finite abelian band.

Also, every subdivision of $K_\beta$ is homotopy equivalent to $K_\beta$, hence
\[
H_1\bigl(N(\mathcal U_\beta^{(m)}),\mathbb Z\bigr)=0,
\qquad
H_2\bigl(N(\mathcal U_\beta^{(m)}),\mathbb Z\bigr)\cong \mathbb Z^\beta
\]
for every $m$ \cite[Secs.~2.1, 2.2]{Hatcher2002}. This records exactly
the finite-nerve hypotheses needed by the realization theorems.

Now assume \textup{(i)}. The finite-abelian interface is
\Cref{lem:bouquet-cover-classical-interface}(iv): it gives a direct-sum
decomposition
\[
G=G_1\oplus G_2
\]
with $G_1,G_2$ nonzero and
\[
d(G_1)\le\beta,
\qquad
d(G_2)\le\beta.
\]
The mixed-realization transfer
\Cref{lem:bouquet-mixed-realization-transfer} applied to these two
summands produces a realization with two visible branches, non-neutral
component gerbes, and $K_{v_i}=G_i$. Because the summands form an
internal direct sum, $G_1\cap G_2=0$ and $G_1+G_2=G$, so condition
\textup{(ii)} follows.

Conversely, assume \textup{(ii)} and put
\[
K_i:=K_{v_i}
\qquad
(i=1,2).
\]
For each $i$, choose a finite nerve presentation of the branch class $\omega_{v_i}$ on one of the covers $\mathcal U_\beta^{(m_i)}$. Since the good-cover interface gives
\[
H_2\bigl(N(\mathcal U_\beta^{(m_i)}),\mathbb Z\bigr)\cong \mathbb Z^\beta,
\]
the hidden subgroup
\[
K_i=\operatorname{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_{\omega_{v_i}})
\]
is generated by at most $\beta$ elements. The equalities
\[
K_1\cap K_2=0,
\qquad
K_1+K_2=G
\]
give an internal direct-sum decomposition
\[
G\cong K_1\oplus K_2
\]
with both summands nonzero. Hence $G$ is decomposable, and the finite abelian indecomposable groups are exactly the cyclic $p$-groups \cite[Chap.~12]{DummitFoote2004}. Moreover
\[
d(G)\le d(K_1)+d(K_2)\le 2\beta.
\]
Thus \textup{(i)} holds.

Finally, the exact-sequence consequences are separate from the realization step. The identities
\[
\bigcap_{i=1}^2 K_{v_i}=0,
\qquad
\sum_{i=1}^2 K_{v_i}=G
\]
give
\[
A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{br}}(r)\cong B_{\mathrm{res}}(r)\cong G,
\qquad
A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{unif}}(r)=0
\]
by \Cref{thm:branch-sensitive-visible-quotient,thm:branch-uniform-visible-quotient,thm:branch-comparison-exact-sequence}. Since both branches are non-neutral, \Cref{thm:mixed-branch-realization}(iv) gives
\[
M,p\Vdash \Null_s^{\mathrm{glue}}(r).
\]
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Exact subgroup classification on torsion-free second homology]\label{cor:torsion-free-h2-classification}
Assume the full hypothesis package of \Cref{thm:mixed-branch-realization}: a
fixed finite nerve $N=N(\mathcal U)$ in a formal \v{C}ech good-cover site,
a trivialized constant finite abelian band $A$, the Leray comparison
isomorphism for the finite-nerve classes, the constructed realization
prestack, and global conservativity at the terminal fibre. Assume
in addition that
\[
H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong \mathbb Z^\beta
\]
for some integer $\beta\ge 0$. Let $(K_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ be a family of subgroups of $A$. Then the following are equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item There exist a state $p$, an admitted reference $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ on the fixed nerve $N$, and a bijection
\[
\Vis_{p,s}(r)\cong \Lambda
\]
such that the branch indexed by $\lambda$ has finite-nerve-class hidden subgroup
\[
K_\lambda.
\]
\item Every subgroup $K_\lambda$ is generated by at most $\beta$ elements.
\end{enumerate}
When these conditions hold,
\[
A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{br}}(r)\cong A\Big/\bigcap_{\lambda\in\Lambda}K_\lambda,
\qquad
A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{unif}}(r)\cong A\Big/\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}K_\lambda,
\]
and
\[
M,p\Vdash \Sec_s(r)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
K_\lambda=0\ \text{for some}\ \lambda\in\Lambda.
\]
In particular, a single branch realizes maximal collapse
\[
K_\omega=A
\]
if and only if $A$ is generated by at most $\beta$ elements. For $\beta=1$, the realizable single-branch finite-nerve-class hidden subgroups are exactly the cyclic subgroups of $A$.
\end{corollary}

\]
with

\]

sec_branch_aggregation.tex:1:\section{Comparison of branches and realization}\label{sec:branch-aggregation}
sec_branch_aggregation.tex:3:We compare the quotients attached to the different visible branches of a single admitted reference. main.tex:70:We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre; with $H^1$-vanishing this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf there. Hence gluing-level nullity cannot be recovered from a strict functorial choice of local representatives. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a canonical Giraud class in $H^2$. For finite abelian bands this yields a homological evaluation map whose image controls a presentation-object visible-quotient invariant, while the character-blind case is exactly the pure $\operatorname{Ext}$ contribution. On fixed finite nerves with $H_1=0$ and $H_2\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, mixed realizations produce precisely the hidden subgroups generated by at most $\beta$ elements; on bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.
sec_introduction.tex:3:Sheaf-theoretic semantics offers a natural language for the passage from local data to global objects. In logical applications, and in particular in sheaf-theoretic analyses of contextuality \cite{AbramskyBrandenburger2011,AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012,AbramskyBarbosaKishidaLalMansfield2015,Caru2017,Caru2018,Montanhano2021}, the central question is whether compatible local families glue to global sections. The classical tools for measuring the failure of gluing are gerbes, obstruction classes, and cohomological invariants \cite{Giraud1971,Breen2006,Hatcher2002}. In this paper we study that question in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations, with the aim of separating the successive layers at which genuinely new local-to-global structure appears.
sec_introduction.tex:14:The second part begins once the set-valued local-object functor is enriched by groupoid-valued data. \Cref{thm:canonical-lift-rigidity} gives a rigidity statement for representative-rigid lifts: if the local-object presheaf is slice-separated and a realization prestack admits a strict functorial choice of representatives and is globally conservative at the terminal fibre, then the sheafification unit is surjective there; under $H^1$-vanishing and the same slice-separatedness, this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf at the terminal fibre. Thus gluing-level nullity is necessarily tied to genuinely gluing-sensitive lift data. \Cref{thm:intrinsic-branch-obstruction-extension} identifies the canonicity that survives at this level: once the sheafified local object functor has been lifted to a banded realization stack, the branch obstruction map to derived $H^2$ is intrinsic up to equivalence of banded extensions. For such an extension, visible value classes are the global sections of the sheaf of connected components (\Cref{thm:visible-value-components}), each visible branch determines a banded component gerbe (\Cref{thm:component-gerbe-decomposition}), and, on slice-separated reference slices, \Cref{thm:gerbe-null-semantics} identifies gluing-level absence with the existence of visible branches together with non-neutrality of the corresponding component gerbes. No general existence theorem for gluing-sensitive lifts is proved; Appendix~\ref{sec:appendix-ghz} gives an explicit GHZ/Mermin example of chosen lift data.
