sec_introduction.tex:14:The second part begins once the set-valued local-object functor is enriched by groupoid-valued data. \Cref{thm:canonical-lift-rigidity} gives a rigidity statement for representative-rigid lifts: if the local-object presheaf is slice-separated and a realization prestack admits a strict functorial choice of representatives and is globally conservative at the terminal fibre, then the sheafification unit is surjective there; under $H^1$-vanishing and the same slice-separatedness, this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf at the terminal fibre. Thus gluing-level nullity is necessarily tied to genuinely gluing-sensitive lift data. \Cref{thm:intrinsic-branch-obstruction-extension} identifies the canonicity that survives at this level: once the sheafified local object functor has been lifted to a banded realization stack, the branch obstruction map to derived $H^2$ is intrinsic up to equivalence of banded extensions. For such an extension, visible value classes are the global sections of the sheaf of connected components (\Cref{thm:visible-value-components}), each visible branch determines a banded component gerbe (\Cref{thm:component-gerbe-decomposition}), and, on slice-separated reference slices, \Cref{thm:gerbe-null-semantics} identifies gluing-level absence with the existence of visible branches together with non-neutrality of the corresponding component gerbes. No general existence theorem for gluing-sensitive lifts is proved; Appendix~\ref{sec:appendix-ghz} gives an explicit GHZ/Mermin example of chosen lift data.

main.tex:58:\title[Gluing Obstructions and Homological Visibility]{Gluing Obstructions and Homological Visibility in a State-Forcing Semantics}
main.tex:70:We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre; with $H^1$-vanishing this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf there. Hence gluing-level nullity cannot be recovered from a strict functorial choice of local representatives. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a canonical Giraud class in $H^2$. For finite abelian bands this yields a homological evaluation map whose image controls a presentation-object visible-quotient invariant, while the character-blind case is exactly the pure $\operatorname{Ext}$ contribution. On fixed finite nerves with $H_1=0$ and $H_2\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, mixed realizations produce precisely the hidden subgroups generated by at most $\beta$ elements; on bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.
main.tex:73:\keywords{state forcing, local objects, sheafification, gerbes, visible quotient, universal coefficient theorem}

sec_introduction.tex:3:Sheaf-theoretic semantics offers a natural language for the passage from local data to global objects. In logical applications, and in particular in sheaf-theoretic analyses of contextuality \cite{AbramskyBrandenburger2011,AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012,AbramskyBarbosaKishidaLalMansfield2015,Caru2017,Caru2018,Montanhano2021}, the central question is whether compatible local families glue to global sections. The classical tools for measuring the failure of gluing are gerbes, obstruction classes, and cohomological invariants \cite{Giraud1971,Breen2006,Hatcher2002}. In this paper we study that question in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations, with the aim of separating the successive layers at which genuinely new local-to-global structure appears.
sec_introduction.tex:9:where $\mathbb{L}_0$ is the pointwise layer, $\mathbb{L}_1$ is the information-state forcing layer, $\mathbb{L}_2$ adds local objects and site structure, $\mathbb{L}_3$ adds branchwise obstruction data, and $\mathbb{L}_4$ adds refinement dynamics. The map $\mathbb{L}_0\hookrightarrow\mathbb{L}_1$ is a singleton semantic embedding, whereas the later steps are conservative extensions in the sense of \Cref{def:conservative-extension}. Thus the geometric and homological material introduced later does not alter the forcing behaviour of formulas already present in the lower layers.
sec_introduction.tex:12:The first part of the paper concerns the passage from information states to local objects. \Cref{prop:compsec-to-sheafification} shows that compatible local sectionability gives nonemptiness of the associated sheafification, and \Cref{thm:sheafification-characterization} proves the converse on slice-separated reference slices. We then prove in \Cref{thm:pointwise-irreducibility} that the predicates $\CompSec_s$, $\Sec_s$, and $\Null^{\mathrm{glue}}_s$ are not definable by automorphism-invariant, constant-free formulas of the $\mathbb{L}_1$-reduct with one free reference variable. This is only a lower-bound statement for the comparison fragment under consideration, but it isolates a genuine change of behaviour between $\mathbb L_1$ and $\mathbb L_2$.
sec_introduction.tex:14:The second part begins once the set-valued local-object functor is enriched by groupoid-valued data. \Cref{thm:canonical-lift-rigidity} gives a rigidity statement for representative-rigid lifts: if the local-object presheaf is slice-separated and a realization prestack admits a strict functorial choice of representatives and is globally conservative at the terminal fibre, then the sheafification unit is surjective there; under $H^1$-vanishing and the same slice-separatedness, this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf at the terminal fibre. Thus gluing-level nullity is necessarily tied to genuinely gluing-sensitive lift data. \Cref{thm:intrinsic-branch-obstruction-extension} identifies the canonicity that survives at this level: once the sheafified local object functor has been lifted to a banded realization stack, the branch obstruction map to derived $H^2$ is intrinsic up to equivalence of banded extensions. For such an extension, visible value classes are the global sections of the sheaf of connected components (\Cref{thm:visible-value-components}), each visible branch determines a banded component gerbe (\Cref{thm:component-gerbe-decomposition}), and, on slice-separated reference slices, \Cref{thm:gerbe-null-semantics} identifies gluing-level absence with the existence of visible branches together with non-neutrality of the corresponding component gerbes. No general existence theorem for gluing-sensitive lifts is proved; Appendix~\ref{sec:appendix-ghz} gives an explicit GHZ/Mermin example of chosen lift data.

main.tex:58:\title[Gluing Obstructions and Homological Visibility]{Gluing Obstructions and Homological Visibility in a State-Forcing Semantics}
main.tex:70:We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre; with $H^1$-vanishing this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf there. Hence gluing-level nullity cannot be recovered from a strict functorial choice of local representatives. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a canonical Giraud class in $H^2$. For finite abelian bands this yields a homological evaluation map whose image controls a presentation-object visible-quotient invariant, while the character-blind case is exactly the pure $\operatorname{Ext}$ contribution. On fixed finite nerves with $H_1=0$ and $H_2\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, mixed realizations produce precisely the hidden subgroups generated by at most $\beta$ elements; on bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.

main.tex:70:We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. A referee reads that as design, not discovery.

The assessment named one lever that would change this:

  Prove that every finite Abramsky-Brandenburger empirical model E canonically, and functorially for refinements, determines a banded realization stack of the kind this paper studies.

## Instruction Priority

Superpowers skills override default system prompt behavior, but **user instructions always take precedence**:

1. **User's explicit instructions** (CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, AGENTS.md, direct requests) Ã¢â‚¬â€ highest priority
2. **Superpowers skills** Ã¢â‚¬â€ override default system behavior where they conflict
3. **Default system prompt** Ã¢â‚¬â€ lowest priority

If CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, or AGENTS.md says "don't use TDD" and a skill says "always use TDD," follow the user's instructions. The user is in control.

## How to Access Skills

**In Claude Code:** Use the `Skill` tool. When you invoke a skill, its content is loaded and presented to youÃ¢â‚¬â€follow it directly. Never use the Read tool on skill files.

**In Copilot CLI:** Use the `skill` tool. Skills are auto-discovered from installed plugins. The `skill` tool works the same as Claude Code's `Skill` tool.

**In Gemini CLI:** Skills activate via the `activate_skill` tool. Gemini loads skill metadata at session start and activates the full content on demand.

**In other environments:** Check your platform's documentation for how skills are loaded.

## Platform Adaptation

Skills use Claude Code tool names. Non-CC platforms: see `references/copilot-tools.md` (Copilot CLI), `references/codex-tools.md` (Codex) for tool equivalents. Gemini CLI users get the tool mapping loaded automatically via GEMINI.md.

# Using Skills

## The Rule

**Invoke relevant or requested skills BEFORE any response or action.** Even a 1% chance a skill might apply means that you should invoke the skill to check. If an invoked skill turns out to be wrong for the situation, you don't need to use it.

+# Terminology audit
+
+## Executive summary (8 lines)
+
+1. I count **68 coined or non-standard term families**: 29 directly collide with established usage, 27 are opaque coinages without a direct collision, and 12 are standard or substantially aligned.
+2. The count is by conceptual family, not spelling: for example, `visible value`, `visible branch`, and `visible quotient` are separate, while singular/plural and adjectival variants are not.
+3. The most damaging collision is **realization**: it denotes assignments, groupoid-valued lifts, existence constructions, and geometric realization, while a logician expects realization of a formula or type.
+4. The second is **state forcing**: the relation is ordinary pointwise satisfaction by every assignment in a set, not set-theoretic, Kripke, Beth, or Kripke-Joyal forcing.
+5. The third is the **visible/hidden/branch** family: it renames global sections of a component sheaf, images of homomorphisms, and quotients by those images without a stable mathematical meaning of visibility.
+6. `slice` is used correctly for the category-theoretic slice, and `bouquet` correctly for a wedge of spheres; their compounds are opaque, but the base terms should not be renamed.
+7. Only a small core is load-bearing: the packaged lift hypothesis, representative-rigidity, the two aggregate quotients, their comparison kernel, and controlled transport among finite presentations.
+8. **Verdict:** the vocabulary is predominantly idiosyncratic naming of standard objects and maps; the genuinely new structures do not require most of it.
+
+## Scope and method
+
+This is a terminology audit, not a mathematical correctness review. I inspected all 52 `definition` environments and also searched theorem titles and prose for terms introduced only by use. Locations are source locations in compilation order. "Formal" means a displayed definition environment; "informal" means that prose or a theorem eventually pins down the meaning; "no" means that the paper never gives that expression its own definition. The audit groups variants that denote the same construction, but it does not group mathematically different uses merely because they share a word.
+
+The collision column uses three labels:
+
+- **C**: direct collision or materially misleading reuse of established terminology;
+- **O**: opaque/local coinage, but no single established meaning is displaced;
+- **A**: standard or substantially aligned usage.
+
+The last column is also the renaming proposal for every **C** entry. For **O** entries it gives the clearest standard-language replacement. Terms marked **A** should normally be retained.
+
+## Complete inventory
+

+

+## Detailed collision analysis
+
+### 1. `realization` is internally inconsistent
+
+The manuscript does not merely differ from one external convention. It uses the same word in four incompatible internal roles:
+
+| Occurrence | Actual object | Standard reading |
+|---|---|---|
+| `R_p` is a set of realizations | Variable assignments in a many-sorted structure | In model theory, a tuple/model realizes a formula or type. |
+| `realization prestack`, `realization-stack extension` | A banded category fibred in groupoids with prescribed `pi_0` | A category theorist expects a moduli/realization construction, not an arbitrary lift package. |
+| `realization theorem`, `mixed realizations` | Existence of deliberately constructed typed expansions with prescribed maps | A model theorist expects a theorem about realizing types, diagrams, or theories. |
+| geometric realization `|K|` | The standard topological realization of a simplicial complex | This is the one standard topological use, but it is buried among the other three. |
+
+This is the single largest impediment to reading. It occurs 198 times and infects theorem statements, hypotheses, and the abstract. The repair must be sense-by-sense, not a global search-and-replace.
+
+### 2. `forcing` announces the wrong semantics
+
+Definition `state-forcing` is exactly universal Tarskian satisfaction over a nonempty team. There are no recursive forcing clauses; quantifiers are evaluated pointwise before the universal quantification over assignments. The manuscript acknowledges this in Remark `flat-forcing-convention`, but only after the title, abstract, introduction, and notation have already activated the standard meanings of forcing. A logician will reasonably test conjunction, disjunction, implication, and quantifier clauses as if this were Kripke-Joyal, Beth, intuitionistic Kripke, or set-theoretic forcing. Calling it **universal team satisfaction** makes the persistence theorem immediate and correctly locates the work relative to team semantics.
+
+### 3. `visible`, `hidden`, and `branch` do not denote one invariant idea
+
+The paper uses "visible" for at least three levels:
+
+1. a terminal section of a sheafification/component sheaf;
+2. a quotient by the subgroup generated by coordinates of a chosen cocycle;
+3. a cokernel of the universal-coefficient evaluation map.
+
+These are related by maps and sometimes surjections, but they are not the same construction. "Hidden" then means the subgroup killed by the relevant quotient, while "branch" means a global component section. A reader from contextuality may take "visible" to mean empirically observable/support-compatible; a topologist may take a branch to be a local analytic branch; a logician may take it to be a path through a Kripke/tree model. The words therefore hide the actual standard objects. The paper should name `aF(a)`, `Im(ev_omega)`, `coker(ev_omega)`, `intersection K_v`, and `sum K_v` directly.
+
+### 4. `slice`: correct base word, nonstandard compound
+
+Here `C_a=C_{p,s}/a` really is the category-theoretic slice, and the topology is restricted to it. A category theorist's initial reading is therefore correct. The trouble is stylistic:
+
+- "slice-separated reference slices" in the abstract is not standard English or standard category theory;
+- `slice-separated` sounds like a new categorical separation axiom;
+- `reference slice` is used before `a=[r]_p` and `C/a` are explained.
+
+The exact standard statement is: **the restricted presheaf `F|_{C/a}` is separated**. Keep `slice`; delete the coined adjective.
+
+### 5. `bouquet`: correct topology, opaque site name
+
+In topology, a bouquet is a wedge sum. The manuscript's `K_beta` has geometric realization homotopy equivalent to `wedge_{j=1}^beta S^2`, so this use is correct. A specialist would not misread the base word once that equation appears. The abstract, however, says "bouquet good covers" without saying what is wedged, and "bouquet site" makes the site sound canonical when it is a specifically generated intersection site from chosen barycentric open-star covers. Retain **bouquet** after the phrase **wedge of `beta` 2-spheres**; rename only the generated site.
+
+### 6. Other collisions that change mathematical expectations
+
+- **Conservative extension:** standard consequence conservativity is not the same as preservation of satisfaction on reducts of the higher models. Without an expansion/exhaustivity result for lower models, the former does not follow from the displayed definition.
+- **Globally conservative:** the definition is essential surjectivity, whereas a conservative functor reflects isomorphisms.
+- **Pure extension:** already means a short exact sequence that is pure in module/abelian-group theory. The paper means membership in the `Ext` summand/kernel in the universal coefficient sequence.
+- **Intrinsic:** the quotients are only controlled relative to finite presentations and chosen comparison zigzags, with no path independence. "Intrinsic" overstates the result.
+- **Strictification:** the four "codes" are injective set maps into a product with an auxiliary finite set. No weak categorical structure is made strict.
+- **Null/total:** a single readout classified as null can have no sheafified value or multiple sheafified values; neither is a null object or a zero value, and "total" only means existence of a global section.
+- **Amplitude lift:** its definition supplies a banded groupoid lift of a support presheaf, not numerical amplitudes, a Hilbert-space vector, normalization, or Born probabilities.
+
+## Load-bearing versus replaceable vocabulary
+
+### Genuinely load-bearing concepts
+
+These concepts do real organizational work and merit short names, although most proposed names should be more descriptive:
+
+| Concept | Why it is load-bearing | Recommended retained name |
+|---|---|---|
+| Weak singleton boundary from point assignments to teams | It distinguishes the first layer transition from the later reduct-preserving expansions. | `singleton-state embedding` |
+| Four-part banded lift hypothesis | It bundles exactly the extra, noncanonical structure on which the gerbe results depend. | `gluing-sensitive banded lift datum` |
+| Strictly pullback-stable representatives | It is the substantive rigidity hypothesis in the no-go result. | `pullback-stable representative choice` (optionally abbreviate `representative-rigid`) |
+| Controlled comparison of finite presentations | It records dependence on chosen refinements and the absence of path independence. | `presentation-comparison groupoid` |
+| Quotient using `intersection_v K_v` | It records information available when the component label is retained. | `label-aware quotient` |
+| Quotient using `sum_v K_v` | It records the characters common to all components. | `common-character quotient` |
+| Kernel `(sum K_v)/(intersection K_v)` | It is the actual new comparison invariant behind the final classification. | `component-forgetting kernel` |
+
+### Standard objects given new names
+
+The following are not new objects: a nonempty team of assignments; universal team satisfaction; a thin site; a presheaf; a separated restriction to a slice; plus-construction representatives; a section of a sheafification; a category fibred in groupoids; stackification; essential surjectivity; a full component substack; a banded gerbe and its Giraud class; a Cech cocycle; the subgroup generated by its values; the UCT map `H^2 -> Hom(H_2,A)`; its image and cokernel; annihilators under Pontryagin duality; `A/(intersection K_v)`; `A/(sum K_v)`; and a set-theoretic injection separating quotient fibers. Renaming these objects does not simplify new mathematics; it makes familiar mathematics harder to recognize.
+
+### Terms that should not be renamed
+
+- **slice category/site:** used correctly for `C/a`.
+- **bouquet:** used correctly for a wedge sum, provided the spheres are stated at first occurrence.
+- **information state:** reasonably aligned with a nonempty set of possible assignments, especially if "team" is supplied as a synonym.
+- **presheaf, sheafification, prestack, stackification, band, banded gerbe, neutral gerbe, Giraud class, Cech nerve, good cover, universal coefficient sequence, `Ext`, annihilator, cokernel:** these are standard and should remain the fixed vocabulary around which the paper is rewritten.
+- **component gerbe:** retainable once `visible branch` is replaced by `global component section`; it accurately describes the full gerbe over one connected-component section.
+
+## Proposed glossary after the introduction
+
+This is the short glossary the revised paper would need after the introduction. It intentionally maps retained abbreviations to standard language rather than reproducing the 68-item audit.
+
+| Retained term | Standard-language meaning |
+|---|---|
+| information state `p=(Gamma,R)` | A nonempty team `R` of assignments with common finite context `Gamma`. |
+| singleton-state embedding | The map sending an assignment to its singleton team, preserving ordinary satisfaction. |
+| admissible parameter `r` | An element satisfying the primitive predicate `Adm_s`; the paper must separately state what admissibility is intended to encode. |
+| base object `a_{p,r}` | The object `[r]_p` of the thin site associated to state `p` and parameter `r`. |
+| reference-refinement site `C_{p,s}` | The thin category of base objects ordered by refinement, equipped with the specified Grothendieck pretopology and pullbacks. |
+| presheaf of local sections `F_{p,s}` | The functor `C_{p,s}^{op}->Set`. |
+| matching-without-amalgamation at `a` | A matching family exists on a cover of `a`, but `F(a)` is empty. |
+| global component section `v` | An element of `pi_0(L_r)(a)`, identified with a section of the sheafification `(aF)(a)`. |
+| component gerbe `G_v` | The full banded substack whose objects lie over the component section `v`. |
+| component obstruction class `omega_v` | The Giraud class `[G_v] in H^2(C/a,A)`. |
+| gluing-sensitive banded lift datum | A banded groupoid lift, its stackification/component-sheaf identification, terminal essential surjectivity, and a Cech-to-derived comparison hypothesis. |
+| homological image `K_omega` | `Im(ev_omega)`, where `ev_omega:H_2(N,Z)->A` is the UCT evaluation of `omega`. |
+| homological cokernel `Q_omega` | `coker(ev_omega)=A/K_omega`. |
+| label-aware quotient | `A/(intersection_v K_v)`, equivalently the image in the product of componentwise quotients. |
+| common-character quotient | `A/(sum_v K_v)`, the quotient detected by characters annihilating every `K_v`. |
+| component-forgetting kernel | The kernel of the canonical map from the label-aware quotient to the common-character quotient, namely `(sum_v K_v)/(intersection_v K_v)`. |
+| presentation-comparison groupoid | The groupoid freely generated by the specified refinements, cocycle replacements, band retrivializations, and their formal inverses. |
+
+## Draft abstract (139 words)
+
+A nonzero finite abelian group `G` occurs as the kernel of the canonical map from the label-aware quotient to the quotient detected uniformly across two component sections, for the chosen good-cover models of a wedge of `beta` 2-spheres, exactly when `d(G) <= 2 beta` and `G` is not a cyclic `p`-group. We obtain this classification from the universal coefficient sequence after fixing a finite nerve, a constant finite abelian band, and a banded groupoid lift of a presheaf. For a component-gerbe class `omega`, evaluation on `H_2` gives a homomorphism `ev_omega:H_2(N,Z)->A`; its image and cokernel determine the componentwise and aggregate quotients. When `H_1(N,Z)=0` and `H_2(N,Z)=Z^beta`, the possible image subgroups are exactly those generated by at most `beta` elements. We also identify matching families without global amalgamations with non-neutral component gerbes under explicit separatedness, effectivity, and Cech-to-derived comparison hypotheses.
+
+## Editorial verdict
+
+The editor's complaint is justified at the level of readability even before mathematical evaluation. Core results can be stated almost entirely with standard terms: teams, presheaves, matching families, slice sites, separatedness, stackification, component gerbes, Giraud classes, the universal-coefficient evaluation map, images, cokernels, intersections, sums, and kernels. The few new comparison constructions become easier, not harder, to see once the metaphorical vocabulary is removed.

+# Terminology audit
+
+## Executive summary (8 lines)
+
+1. I count **68 coined or non-standard term families**: 29 directly collide with established usage, 27 are opaque coinages without a direct collision, and 12 are standard or substantially aligned.
+2. The count is by conceptual family, not spelling: for example, `visible value`, `visible branch`, and `visible quotient` are separate, while singular/plural and adjectival variants are not.
+3. The most damaging collision is **realization**: it denotes assignments, groupoid-valued lifts, existence constructions, and geometric realization, while a logician expects realization of a formula or type.
+4. The second is **state forcing**: the relation is ordinary pointwise satisfaction by every assignment in a set, not set-theoretic, Kripke, Beth, or Kripke-Joyal forcing.
+5. The third is the **visible/hidden/branch** family: it renames global sections of a component sheaf, images of homomorphisms, and quotients by those images without a stable mathematical meaning of visibility.
+6. `slice` is used correctly for the category-theoretic slice, and `bouquet` correctly for a wedge of spheres; their compounds are opaque, but the base terms should not be renamed.
+7. Only a small core is load-bearing: the packaged lift hypothesis, representative-rigidity, the two aggregate quotients, their comparison kernel, and controlled transport among finite presentations.
+8. **Verdict:** the vocabulary is predominantly idiosyncratic naming of standard objects and maps; the genuinely new structures do not require most of it.
+
+## Scope and method
+
+This is a terminology audit, not a mathematical correctness review. I inspected all 52 `definition` environments and also searched theorem titles and prose for terms introduced only by use. Locations are source locations in compilation order. "Formal" means a displayed definition environment; "informal" means that prose or a theorem eventually pins down the meaning; "no" means that the paper never gives that expression its own definition. The audit groups variants that denote the same construction, but it does not group mathematically different uses merely because they share a word.
+
+The collision column uses three labels:
+
+- **C**: direct collision or materially misleading reuse of established terminology;
+- **O**: opaque/local coinage, but no single established meaning is displaced;
+- **A**: standard or substantially aligned usage.
+
+The last column is also the renaming proposal for every **C** entry. For **O** entries it gives the clearest standard-language replacement. Terms marked **A** should normally be retained.
+

+
+## Detailed collision analysis
+
+### 1. `realization` is internally inconsistent
+
+The manuscript does not merely differ from one external convention. It uses the same word in four incompatible internal roles:
+
+| Occurrence | Actual object | Standard reading |
+|---|---|---|
+| `R_p` is a set of realizations | Variable assignments in a many-sorted structure | In model theory, a tuple/model realizes a formula or type. |
+| `realization prestack`, `realization-stack extension` | A banded category fibred in groupoids with prescribed `pi_0` | A category theorist expects a moduli/realization construction, not an arbitrary lift package. |
+| `realization theorem`, `mixed realizations` | Existence of deliberately constructed typed expansions with prescribed maps | A model theorist expects a theorem about realizing types, diagrams, or theories. |
+| geometric realization `|K|` | The standard topological realization of a simplicial complex | This is the one standard topological use, but it is buried among the other three. |
+
+This is the single largest impediment to reading. It occurs 198 times and infects theorem statements, hypotheses, and the abstract. The repair must be sense-by-sense, not a global search-and-replace.
+
+### 2. `forcing` announces the wrong semantics
+
+Definition `state-forcing` is exactly universal Tarskian satisfaction over a nonempty team. There are no recursive forcing clauses; quantifiers are evaluated pointwise before the universal quantification over assignments. The manuscript acknowledges this in Remark `flat-forcing-convention`, but only after the title, abstract, introduction, and notation have already activated the standard meanings of forcing. A logician will reasonably test conjunction, disjunction, implication, and quantifier clauses as if this were Kripke-Joyal, Beth, intuitionistic Kripke, or set-theoretic forcing. Calling it **universal team satisfaction** makes the persistence theorem immediate and correctly locates the work relative to team semantics.
+
+### 3. `visible`, `hidden`, and `branch` do not denote one invariant idea
+
+The paper uses "visible" for at least three levels:
+
+1. a terminal section of a sheafification/component sheaf;
+2. a quotient by the subgroup generated by coordinates of a chosen cocycle;
+3. a cokernel of the universal-coefficient evaluation map.
+
+These are related by maps and sometimes surjections, but they are not the same construction. "Hidden" then means the subgroup killed by the relevant quotient, while "branch" means a global component section. A reader from contextuality may take "visible" to mean empirically observable/support-compatible; a topologist may take a branch to be a local analytic branch; a logician may take it to be a path through a Kripke/tree model. The words therefore hide the actual standard objects. The paper should name `aF(a)`, `Im(ev_omega)`, `coker(ev_omega)`, `intersection K_v`, and `sum K_v` directly.
+
+### 4. `slice`: correct base word, nonstandard compound
+
+Here `C_a=C_{p,s}/a` really is the category-theoretic slice, and the topology is restricted to it. A category theorist's initial reading is therefore correct. The trouble is stylistic:
+
+- "slice-separated reference slices" in the abstract is not standard English or standard category theory;
+- `slice-separated` sounds like a new categorical separation axiom;
+- `reference slice` is used before `a=[r]_p` and `C/a` are explained.
+
+The exact standard statement is: **the restricted presheaf `F|_{C/a}` is separated**. Keep `slice`; delete the coined adjective.
+
+### 5. `bouquet`: correct topology, opaque site name
+
+In topology, a bouquet is a wedge sum. The manuscript's `K_beta` has geometric realization homotopy equivalent to `wedge_{j=1}^beta S^2`, so this use is correct. A specialist would not misread the base word once that equation appears. The abstract, however, says "bouquet good covers" without saying what is wedged, and "bouquet site" makes the site sound canonical when it is a specifically generated intersection site from chosen barycentric open-star covers. Retain **bouquet** after the phrase **wedge of `beta` 2-spheres**; rename only the generated site.
+
+### 6. Other collisions that change mathematical expectations
+
+- **Conservative extension:** standard consequence conservativity is not the same as preservation of satisfaction on reducts of the higher models. Without an expansion/exhaustivity result for lower models, the former does not follow from the displayed definition.
+- **Globally conservative:** the definition is essential surjectivity, whereas a conservative functor reflects isomorphisms.
+- **Pure extension:** already means a short exact sequence that is pure in module/abelian-group theory. The paper means membership in the `Ext` summand/kernel in the universal coefficient sequence.
+- **Intrinsic:** the quotients are only controlled relative to finite presentations and chosen comparison zigzags, with no path independence. "Intrinsic" overstates the result.
+- **Strictification:** the four "codes" are injective set maps into a product with an auxiliary finite set. No weak categorical structure is made strict.
+- **Null/total:** a single readout classified as null can have no sheafified value or multiple sheafified values; neither is a null object or a zero value, and "total" only means existence of a global section.
+- **Amplitude lift:** its definition supplies a banded groupoid lift of a support presheaf, not numerical amplitudes, a Hilbert-space vector, normalization, or Born probabilities.
+
+## Load-bearing versus replaceable vocabulary
+
+### Genuinely load-bearing concepts
+
+These concepts do real organizational work and merit short names, although most proposed names should be more descriptive:
+
+| Concept | Why it is load-bearing | Recommended retained name |
+|---|---|---|
+| Weak singleton boundary from point assignments to teams | It distinguishes the first layer transition from the later reduct-preserving expansions. | `singleton-state embedding` |
+| Four-part banded lift hypothesis | It bundles exactly the extra, noncanonical structure on which the gerbe results depend. | `gluing-sensitive banded lift datum` |
+| Strictly pullback-stable representatives | It is the substantive rigidity hypothesis in the no-go result. | `pullback-stable representative choice` (optionally abbreviate `representative-rigid`) |
+| Controlled comparison of finite presentations | It records dependence on chosen refinements and the absence of path independence. | `presentation-comparison groupoid` |
+| Quotient using `intersection_v K_v` | It records information available when the component label is retained. | `label-aware quotient` |
+| Quotient using `sum_v K_v` | It records the characters common to all components. | `common-character quotient` |
+| Kernel `(sum K_v)/(intersection K_v)` | It is the actual new comparison invariant behind the final classification. | `component-forgetting kernel` |
+
+### Standard objects given new names
+
+The following are not new objects: a nonempty team of assignments; universal team satisfaction; a thin site; a presheaf; a separated restriction to a slice; plus-construction representatives; a section of a sheafification; a category fibred in groupoids; stackification; essential surjectivity; a full component substack; a banded gerbe and its Giraud class; a Cech cocycle; the subgroup generated by its values; the UCT map `H^2 -> Hom(H_2,A)`; its image and cokernel; annihilators under Pontryagin duality; `A/(intersection K_v)`; `A/(sum K_v)`; and a set-theoretic injection separating quotient fibers. Renaming these objects does not simplify new mathematics; it makes familiar mathematics harder to recognize.
+
+### Terms that should not be renamed
+
+- **slice category/site:** used correctly for `C/a`.
+- **bouquet:** used correctly for a wedge sum, provided the spheres are stated at first occurrence.
+- **information state:** reasonably aligned with a nonempty set of possible assignments, especially if "team" is supplied as a synonym.
+- **presheaf, sheafification, prestack, stackification, band, banded gerbe, neutral gerbe, Giraud class, Cech nerve, good cover, universal coefficient sequence, `Ext`, annihilator, cokernel:** these are standard and should remain the fixed vocabulary around which the paper is rewritten.
+- **component gerbe:** retainable once `visible branch` is replaced by `global component section`; it accurately describes the full gerbe over one connected-component section.
+
+## Proposed glossary after the introduction
+
+This is the short glossary the revised paper would need after the introduction. It intentionally maps retained abbreviations to standard language rather than reproducing the 68-item audit.
+
+| Retained term | Standard-language meaning |
+|---|---|
+| information state `p=(Gamma,R)` | A nonempty team `R` of assignments with common finite context `Gamma`. |
+| singleton-state embedding | The map sending an assignment to its singleton team, preserving ordinary satisfaction. |
+| admissible parameter `r` | An element satisfying the primitive predicate `Adm_s`; the paper must separately state what admissibility is intended to encode. |
+| base object `a_{p,r}` | The object `[r]_p` of the thin site associated to state `p` and parameter `r`. |
+| reference-refinement site `C_{p,s}` | The thin category of base objects ordered by refinement, equipped with the specified Grothendieck pretopology and pullbacks. |
+| presheaf of local sections `F_{p,s}` | The functor `C_{p,s}^{op}->Set`. |
+| matching-without-amalgamation at `a` | A matching family exists on a cover of `a`, but `F(a)` is empty. |
+| global component section `v` | An element of `pi_0(L_r)(a)`, identified with a section of the sheafification `(aF)(a)`. |
+| component gerbe `G_v` | The full banded substack whose objects lie over the component section `v`. |
+| component obstruction class `omega_v` | The Giraud class `[G_v] in H^2(C/a,A)`. |
+| gluing-sensitive banded lift datum | A banded groupoid lift, its stackification/component-sheaf identification, terminal essential surjectivity, and a Cech-to-derived comparison hypothesis. |
+| homological image `K_omega` | `Im(ev_omega)`, where `ev_omega:H_2(N,Z)->A` is the UCT evaluation of `omega`. |
+| homological cokernel `Q_omega` | `coker(ev_omega)=A/K_omega`. |
+| label-aware quotient | `A/(intersection_v K_v)`, equivalently the image in the product of componentwise quotients. |
+| common-character quotient | `A/(sum_v K_v)`, the quotient detected by characters annihilating every `K_v`. |
+| component-forgetting kernel | The kernel of the canonical map from the label-aware quotient to the common-character quotient, namely `(sum_v K_v)/(intersection_v K_v)`. |
+| presentation-comparison groupoid | The groupoid freely generated by the specified refinements, cocycle replacements, band retrivializations, and their formal inverses. |
+
+## Draft abstract (139 words)
+
+A nonzero finite abelian group `G` occurs as the kernel of the canonical map from the label-aware quotient to the quotient detected uniformly across two component sections, for the chosen good-cover models of a wedge of `beta` 2-spheres, exactly when `d(G) <= 2 beta` and `G` is not a cyclic `p`-group. We obtain this classification from the universal coefficient sequence after fixing a finite nerve, a constant finite abelian band, and a banded groupoid lift of a presheaf. For a component-gerbe class `omega`, evaluation on `H_2` gives a homomorphism `ev_omega:H_2(N,Z)->A`; its image and cokernel determine the componentwise and aggregate quotients. When `H_1(N,Z)=0` and `H_2(N,Z)=Z^beta`, the possible image subgroups are exactly those generated by at most `beta` elements. We also identify matching families without global amalgamations with non-neutral component gerbes under explicit separatedness, effectivity, and Cech-to-derived comparison hypotheses.
+
+## Editorial verdict
+
+The editor's complaint is justified at the level of readability even before mathematical evaluation. Core results can be stated almost entirely with standard terms: teams, presheaves, matching families, slice sites, separatedness, stackification, component gerbes, Giraud classes, the universal-coefficient evaluation map, images, cokernels, intersections, sums, and kernels. The few new comparison constructions become easier, not harder, to see once the metaphorical vocabulary is removed.

# Verification Before Completion

## Overview

Claiming work is complete without verification is dishonesty, not efficiency.

**Core principle:** Evidence before claims, always.

**Violating the letter of this rule is violating the spirit of this rule.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO COMPLETION CLAIMS WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION EVIDENCE
```

If you haven't run the verification command in this message, you cannot claim it passes.

## The Gate Function

```
BEFORE claiming any status or expressing satisfaction:

1. IDENTIFY: What command proves this claim?
2. RUN: Execute the FULL command (fresh, complete)
3. READ: Full output, check exit code, count failures
4. VERIFY: Does output confirm the claim?
   - If NO: State actual status with evidence
   - If YES: State claim WITH evidence
5. ONLY THEN: Make the claim

Skip any step = lying, not verifying
```

## Common Failures

| Claim | Requires | Not Sufficient |
|-------|----------|----------------|
| Tests pass | Test command output: 0 failures | Previous run, "should pass" |
| Linter clean | Linter output: 0 errors | Partial check, extrapolation |
| Build succeeds | Build command: exit 0 | Linter passing, logs look good |
| Bug fixed | Test original symptom: passes | Code changed, assumed fixed |
| Regression test works | Red-green cycle verified | Test passes once |
| Agent completed | VCS diff shows changes | Agent reports "success" |
| Requirements met | Line-by-line checklist | Tests passing |

## Red Flags - STOP

- Using "should", "probably", "seems to"
- Expressing satisfaction before verification ("Great!", "Perfect!", "Done!", etc.)
- About to commit/push/PR without verification
- Trusting agent success reports
- Relying on partial verification
- Thinking "just this once"
- Tired and wanting work over
- **ANY wording implying success without having run verification**

## Rationalization Prevention

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Should work now" | RUN the verification |
| "I'm confident" | Confidence â‰  evidence |
| "Just this once" | No exceptions |
| "Linter passed" | Linter â‰  compiler |
| "Agent said success" | Verify independently |
| "I'm tired" | Exhaustion â‰  excuse |
| "Partial check is enough" | Partial proves nothing |
| "Different words so rule doesn't apply" | Spirit over letter |

+# Terminology audit
+
+## Executive summary (8 lines)
+
+1. I count **68 coined or non-standard term families**: 29 directly collide with established usage, 27 are opaque coinages without a direct collision, and 12 are standard or substantially aligned.
+2. The count is by conceptual family, not spelling: for example, `visible value`, `visible branch`, and `visible quotient` are separate, while singular/plural and adjectival variants are not.
+3. The most damaging collision is **realization**: it denotes assignments, groupoid-valued lifts, existence constructions, and geometric realization, while a logician expects realization of a formula or type.
+4. The second is **state forcing**: the relation is ordinary pointwise satisfaction by every assignment in a set, not set-theoretic, Kripke, Beth, or Kripke-Joyal forcing.
+5. The third is the **visible/hidden/branch** family: it renames global sections of a component sheaf, images of homomorphisms, and quotients by those images without a stable mathematical meaning of visibility.
+6. `slice` is used correctly for the category-theoretic slice, and `bouquet` correctly for a wedge of spheres; their compounds are opaque, but the base terms should not be renamed.
+7. Only a small core is load-bearing: the packaged lift hypothesis, representative-rigidity, the two aggregate quotients, their comparison kernel, and controlled transport among finite presentations.
+8. **Verdict:** the vocabulary is predominantly idiosyncratic naming of standard objects and maps; the genuinely new structures do not require most of it.
+
+## Scope and method
+
+This is a terminology audit, not a mathematical correctness review. I inspected all 52 `definition` environments and also searched theorem titles and prose for terms introduced only by use. Locations are source locations in compilation order. "Formal" means a displayed definition environment; "informal" means that prose or a theorem eventually pins down the meaning; "no" means that the paper never gives that expression its own definition. The audit groups variants that denote the same construction, but it does not group mathematically different uses merely because they share a word.
+
+The collision column uses three labels:
+
+- **C**: direct collision or materially misleading reuse of established terminology;
+- **O**: opaque/local coinage, but no single established meaning is displaced;
+- **A**: standard or substantially aligned usage.
+
+The last column is also the renaming proposal for every **C** entry. For **O** entries it gives the clearest standard-language replacement. Terms marked **A** should normally be retained.
+
+## Complete inventory
+
+### Semantic framework and local sections
+
+| # | Term or family | First use | Defined? | Meaning in this paper | Class; recommended wording |
+|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
+| 1 | `logic layer` | `sec_preliminaries.tex:8` | Formal, Def. `logic-layer` | A signature, formula class, model class, state assignment, forcing relation, and induced consequence relation. | **O**; say **semantic framework** or **semantic signature and model class**. |
+| 2 | `conservative extension` | `sec_introduction.tex:7` | Formal, `sec_preliminaries.tex:24` | An expansion equipped with a forgetful functor and state projection that preserves truth of every lower-language formula on reducts. | **C**; in logic, conservativity means no new lower-language consequences. The displayed condition does not by itself give that unless lower models expand. Say **truth-preserving reduct expansion**; reserve "conservative" for consequence conservativity and prove it separately. |
+| 3 | `singleton semantic embedding` | `sec_introduction.tex:7` | Formal, `sec_preliminaries.tex:50` | Point assignments embed as singleton sets of assignments, preserving lower-language satisfaction only on that image. | **O**; **singleton-state embedding** states the content. |
+| 4 | `generated/admissible expansion (model class/convention)` | `sec_preliminaries.tex:136` | Informal convention plus Prop. `admissible-layer-expansion-interface` at line 197 | Any supplied, well-typed higher-layer data are declared to form an admissible higher model while the reduct is fixed. | **C**; model theorists expect admissibility to be an independently specified property, not membership generated by the construction. Say **freely generated expansion class** or **class of all typed expansions**. |
+| 5 | `information state` | `sec_introduction.tex:7` | Formal, `sec_information_states.tex:21` | A nonempty set of assignments in a fixed finite context. | **A**; this is compatible with information-state/team usage. Add once: "a nonempty team of assignments." |
+| 6 | `state forcing` / `forcing semantics` / `flat forcing` | title, `main.tex:58`; abstract, line 70 | Formal, `sec_information_states.tex:39`; disclaimer at line 48 | `M,p |= phi` iff every assignment in the state's set satisfies `phi` in ordinary Tarskian semantics. | **C**; forcing normally invokes recursive clauses and/or extensions (set-theoretic, Kripke, Beth, or Kripke-Joyal). A specialist will look for those clauses. Say **universal team satisfaction** or **flat satisfaction on teams** throughout, including title and keywords. |
+| 7 | `decidedness` (and `delayed decidability`) | `sec_information_states.tex:63` (`sec_appendix.tex:71` for delayed) | Formal | `phi` or `not phi` holds universally on the team; delayed means neither holds initially but one holds after refinement. | **A** for decidedness; the delayed variant is descriptive. Retain after replacing forcing notation by satisfaction notation. |
+| 8 | `referenceable sort`, `reference sort`, `admitted reference`, `admissibility` | `sec_preliminaries.tex:6`; language introduced `sec_null_decomposition.tex:17-21` | **No semantic definition** of admission; only a primitive sort and predicate `Adm_s` are introduced | A distinguished element `r` of a new sort for which `Adm_s(r)` holds and to which a site/object `a=[r]_p` is attached. | **O**, but critically underexplained. Say **admissible parameter** (or define "reference" operationally before the abstract). State what `Adm_s` asserts and which models determine it. |
+| 9 | `reference class` | `sec_preliminaries.tex:6` | Formal, `sec_null_decomposition.tex:30` | An element `[r]_p` of a stipulated set `R_s(p)`, assigned surjectively to admitted references; no equivalence relation is required. | **O** and structurally misleading: "class" suggests an equivalence class. Say **site object associated to `(p,r)`** or **base object `a_{p,r}`** unless an equivalence relation is supplied. |
+| 10 | `local reference site` / `local reference frame` | `sec_preliminaries.tex:6` | Formal, `sec_null_decomposition.tex:42` (label says frame, title says site) | A small thin category built from the refinement preorder on reference classes, with a Grothendieck pretopology and specified pullbacks. | **O**; **thin site of reference refinements**. Remove the site/frame label mismatch. |
+| 11 | `local object functor` / `local object presheaf` | abstract, `main.tex:70` | Formal, `sec_null_decomposition.tex:77` | An arbitrary contravariant set-valued functor on the thin site. | **C**; in category theory a local object is usually local with respect to a localization/class of morphisms. Here nothing is localized. Say **presheaf of local sections** or simply **presheaf `F`**. |
+| 12 | `local sectionability`, `compatible local sectionability`, `global sectionability`; predicates `LocSec`, `CompSec`, `Sec` | `sec_null_decomposition.tex:3` | Formal together at `sec_null_decomposition.tex:88` | Respectively: a cover has nonempty fibers; a cover has a matching family; the terminal fiber `F(a)` is nonempty. | **A** mathematically, though noun-heavy. Prefer **local nonemptiness**, **existence of a matching family**, and **existence of a global section**. |
+| 13 | `local-object decomposition` / `decomposition decidability` | `sec_null_decomposition_part2.tex:207` | Formal at line 206 | For every admitted parameter of a sort, the local-nonemptiness and matching-family predicates are each decided at a state. | **O**; no object is decomposed. Say **decidability of the two local-section predicates**. |
+| 14 | `automorphism-invariant lower comparison class`, `lower reduct`, `lower fragment`, `pointwise irreducibility` | abstract, `main.tex:70`; formal class at `sec_null_decomposition_part2.tex:321` | Formal for the class; theorem-specific for the rest | Constant-free one-free-reference-variable formulas of the `Sigma_1` reduct, required to be automorphism invariant; used for a non-definability result. | **O**; **automorphism-invariant one-variable fragment of the `Sigma_1` reduct**. "Irreducibility" should be **non-definability**. |
+| 15 | `typed readout`; `undefined`, `total`, `null`; `local/compatibility/gluing null modes` | abstract has gluing nullity, `main.tex:70`; formal at `sec_null_decomposition_part2.tex:77`, 149, 165 | Formal | A three-valued output: inadmissible; the unique sheafified value if exactly one exists; otherwise null. Separately, admitted parameters with no global section are divided according to the first failed stage. | **C**; `total` and `null` have established meanings for functions, objects, morphisms, and nullity. Worse, "null" conflates zero, no value, and multiple values. Use **inadmissible / uniquely determined / non-unique-or-absent**, and **no local sections / no matching family / matching family without global section**. |

+### Slices, lifts, components, and gerbes
+
+| # | Term or family | First use | Defined? | Meaning in this paper | Class; recommended wording |
+|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
+| 16 | `slice`, `slice site`, `reference slice` | abstract, `main.tex:70` | Standard construction displayed at `sec_null_decomposition.tex:140` | The genuine categorical slice site `C_{p,s}/a`, whose terminal object is `a`. | **A** for **slice category/site**. Do not rename it. Replace the unexplained phrase "reference slice" by **the slice site `C_{p,s}/a` associated to `r`** on first use. |
+| 17 | `slice-separated` | abstract, `main.tex:70` | Formal, `sec_null_decomposition.tex:140` | The restriction `F|_{C/a}` is a separated presheaf at every object of the slice. | **O**; this is not a standard property name, but its content is standard. Say **`F|_{C/a}` is separated**. A category theorist may otherwise wonder whether morphisms of slices are being separated. |
+| 18 | `realization` (unqualified) | abstract, `main.tex:70` | **No uniform definition** | At least four meanings occur: an assignment in a team; a local object in a fibred groupoid; an existence construction realizing a prescribed homomorphism/subgroup; and the geometric realization `|K|` of a simplicial complex. | **C, severe**; model theory uses "realizes" for a formula/type, topology uses geometric realization, and all four senses occur here. Use **assignment**, **lift object**, **construct/attain**, and **geometric realization**, respectively. Never use bare "realization" as the umbrella. |
+| 19 | `realization prestack` / `compatible realization stack` | abstract, `main.tex:70` | Formal, `sec_null_decomposition.tex:470` | A category fibred in groupoids whose presheaf of isomorphism classes is `F|_{C/a}` and whose automorphism sheaves are identified with a fixed abelian band; its stackification is `L_r`. | **C** through the overloaded head word and because a prestack is not a stack. Say **banded groupoid lift of `F`** and **its stackification**. |
+| 20 | `gluing-sensitive realization datum/lift` | `sec_introduction.tex:14`; formal `sec_null_decomposition_part2.tex:325` | Formal | A package `(P_r,L_r,A,Cov^acyc)` requiring a banded prestack, a stack with component sheaf `aF`, terminal essential surjectivity, and a Cech-to-derived comparison family. | **O**, and load-bearing. Say **gluing-sensitive banded lift datum**; list its four clauses in the introduction. |
+| 21 | `visible presentation`, `value-equivalent` | `sec_null_decomposition_part2.tex:3-10` | Formal | A plus-construction representative (local sections agreeing after refinements); equivalence is equality after common cover and overlap refinements. | **O**; **plus-construction representative** and **equivalent representatives in `F^+`**. |
+| 22 | `visible value class` / `visible value` | `sec_preliminaries.tex:6`; formal `sec_null_decomposition_part2.tex:3` | Formal, but first used much earlier | An equivalence class of the preceding representatives; later proved to be an element of `(aF)(a)`, equivalently a terminal section of the component sheaf. | **O**; **sheafified global section** or **section of `(aF)(a)`**. It need not be a "value" in any standard semantic sense. |
+| 23 | `visible branch` / `branch label` | abstract, `main.tex:70` | **No separate definition**; used as a synonym for `v in Vis`, then as a component-sheaf section | A global section `v` of `pi_0(L_r)` (identified with `(aF)(a)`), indexing a full component substack/gerbe. | **C**; a logician expects a Kripke/tree branch, a topologist an analytic branch. Say **global component section** or **component label**. |
+| 24 | `globally conservative at the terminal fibre` | abstract, `main.tex:70` | Formal, `sec_null_decomposition.tex:657` | The stackification functor on the terminal fiber `P_r(a) -> L_r(a)` is essentially surjective. | **C**; conservative functors reflect isomorphisms, and conservative extensions preserve consequences. Say **essentially surjective on the terminal fiber**. |
+| 25 | `effective terminal components` / `terminal component effectivity` | `sec_null_decomposition.tex:669` | Formal | Every global section of `pi_0(L_r)` is represented by an actual object of `L_r(a)`. | **C**; effectivity in descent usually concerns descent data, equivalence relations, or epimorphisms. Say **global representability of component sections**. |
+| 26 | `representative-rigid lift` / `representative rigidity` | abstract, `main.tex:70`; formal `sec_null_decomposition.tex:705` | Formal | A split-cleavage choice of one object representing each `F(U)` class, strictly preserved by every pullback. | **O**, and load-bearing. Say **strictly pullback-stable choice of representatives**; `representative-rigid` may remain as an abbreviation after this sentence. |
+| 27 | `Cech-derived comparison package` / hypothesis `(H4)` | `sec_gerbe_obstruction.tex:23` | Formal | A filtered cofinal family of band-trivializing covers for which the colimit of Cech `H^2` is isomorphic to derived sheaf `H^2`. | **O** but precise. Retain only as **Cech-to-derived comparison hypothesis**; "package" is administrative rather than mathematical. |
+| 28 | `component gerbe` | `sec_introduction.tex:14`; formal `sec_gerbe_obstruction.tex:84` | Formal, conditional on the decomposition theorem | The full substack of `L_r` over objects whose connected-component class is the restriction of a fixed global component section `v`; under hypotheses it is a banded gerbe. | **A/O**; **gerbe over a fixed component section** is standard and clear. `component gerbe` is retainable after `v` is renamed. |
+| 29 | `branch obstruction class/map` | abstract, `main.tex:70`; formal class `sec_gerbe_obstruction.tex:84` | Formal for the class; theorem-defined for the map | The Giraud class `[G_v] in H^2(C/a,A)` of the component gerbe, obtained via compatible Cech representatives and comparison. | **O**; **Giraud class of the component gerbe** and **component-section obstruction map**. |
+| 30 | `banded realization-stack extension` | abstract, `main.tex:70`; formal `sec_gerbe_obstruction.tex:110` | Formal | An `A`-banded stack `E_r` together with an isomorphism `pi_0(E_r) ~= aF|_{C/a}`. It is not presented as an extension sequence. | **C**; "extension" suggests an exact/categorical extension, and "realization" is overloaded. Say **banded stack lift of the sheaf `aF`**. |
+| 31 | `v-component substack` | `sec_gerbe_obstruction.tex:133` | Formal within Def. `realization-stack-extension` | The full substack on objects whose component maps to the restriction of `v`. | **A**; **full substack over the component section `v`** is already standard language. |
+| 32 | `gluing failure`, `gluing-level nullity`, `gluing-level absence`, `gluing-null` | abstract, `main.tex:70` | Formal predicate at `sec_null_decomposition_part2.tex:165`; gerbe reformulation at `sec_gerbe_obstruction.tex:716` | An admitted parameter for which a matching family exists but `F(a)` is empty; under extra lift hypotheses, component sections exist but all corresponding gerbes are non-neutral. | **C**; `nullity` normally means kernel dimension and "absence" suggests no local object at all. Say **matching-without-amalgamation** or **failure of effective descent at `a`**, being careful that the paper uses set-valued matching plus extra gerbe hypotheses. |

+### Finite presentations, quotients, characters, and multiple components
+
+| # | Term or family | First use | Defined? | Meaning in this paper | Class; recommended wording |
+|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
+| 33 | `finite obstruction presentation` (with `ordered Cech convention`) | `sec_gerbe_visible_strictification.tex:6`, 30 | Formal | A finite cover, a trivialized finite constant band `A`, and an ordered Cech 2-cocycle `alpha` representing one component-gerbe class. | **A/O**; **finite Cech cocycle representative** is shorter and standard. Keep the ordering convention as notation, not a named object. |
+| 34 | `obstruction subgroup` `H_alpha` | `sec_gerbe_visible_strictification.tex:53` | Formal within Def. at line 30 | The subgroup of `A` generated by the coordinate values `alpha_ijk` of one chosen cocycle representative. | **O** and dangerously presentation-dependent. Say **coordinate-image subgroup of `alpha`**. It is not determined by the cohomology class. |
+| 35 | `visible quotient` (strict/presentation-level) | keywords and abstract, `main.tex:16`, 70; formal `sec_gerbe_visible_strictification.tex:57` | Formal | `A/H_alpha`, the quotient by the subgroup generated by cocycle coordinates. | **O**, central but metaphorical. Say **cocycle-coordinate quotient `A/H_alpha`**. |
+| 36 | `presentation-invariant character` | `sec_gerbe_visible_strictification.tex:108-117` | Formal | A character of `A` that kills `H_alpha`, hence factors through `A/H_alpha`; it is relative to the chosen presentation. | **C**; the name suggests invariance under changing presentations, which is not proved. Say **character annihilating the coordinate-image subgroup**. |
+| 37 | `globally admissible character` / `uniformly admissible character` | `sec_gerbe_visible_strictification.tex:133`; `sec_branch_aggregation.tex:54-59` | Informal/theorem-defined | Respectively, a character whose pushed-forward cocycle is trivial under all coboundary changes considered; or one lying in every component's annihilator. | **O**; **cocycle-trivializing character** and **common annihilating character**. "Globally" is especially unclear about the quantification domain. |
+| 38 | `character channel` | `sec_gerbe_visible_strictification.tex:108` | Informal | A group character `chi:A->T`, treated as a linear detector of quotient classes. | **C**; "channel" has an information-theoretic meaning not supplied here. Say simply **character** or **character-valued observable** if an observation map is actually defined. |
+| 39 | `auxiliary/intrinsic/branch-resolution/branch-preserving strictification code` | first at `sec_gerbe_visible_strictification.tex:203`; later `sec_homological_visibility_intrinsic.tex:617`, `sec_branch_aggregation.tex:245`, 338 | Formal, four variants | A finite set `R` and an injective set map into a quotient times `R`, with first projection the quotient; variants change which quotient(s) must be preserved. | **C**; neither categorical strictification nor coding-theoretic structure is used. +| 40 | `finite nerve presentation` | `sec_introduction.tex:16`; formal `sec_homological_visibility.tex:10` | Formal | A finite cover with finite nerve, a band trivialization, and a class `omega in H^2(N,A)`, plus comparison data if it is also treated as derived sheaf cohomology. | **A/O**; **finite nerve cocycle model** or **finite nerve representative**. |
+| 41 | `homological evaluation map` | abstract, `main.tex:70`; formal `sec_homological_visibility.tex:45` | Formal | The universal-coefficient map `ev_omega = eta_A(omega): H_2(N,Z)->A`. | **A**; retain **evaluation of `omega` on `H_2`**. |
+| 42 | `finite nerve comparison groupoid`, `elementary comparison`, `comparison-equivalent` | `sec_homological_visibility.tex:51` | Formal | Objects are finite presentations; arrows are finite zigzags generated by three chosen comparison operations and formal inverses. +| 43 | `finite-nerve-class hidden subgroup` / `hidden subgroup` | abstract, `main.tex:70`; formal `sec_homological_visibility_intrinsic.tex:3` | Formal | `K_omega = Im(ev_omega) <= A`. | **C**; "hidden subgroup" has established uses in quantum algorithms and harmonic analysis, while nothing is hidden in the definition. +| 44 | `finite-nerve-class/intrinsic visible quotient` | abstract, `main.tex:70`; formal `sec_homological_visibility_intrinsic.tex:3` | Formal | `A_vis^omega = coker(ev_omega)=A/Im(ev_omega)`, invariant only within the chosen finite comparison groupoid. | **O**, but `intrinsic` overstates presentation independence. +| 45 | `class-admissible character` | `sec_homological_visibility_intrinsic.tex:17` | Formal | A character `chi` such that the pushed-forward class `chi_*(omega)` vanishes; equivalently, `chi` annihilates `Im(ev_omega)` under the stated hypotheses. | **O**; **character annihilating the homological image** (or **class-trivializing character**). |
+| 46 | `presentation-object visibility/canonical` | abstract, `main.tex:70`; `sec_homological_visibility.tex:117`; `sec_homological_visibility_intrinsic.tex:185` | Informal | The claim that `K_omega` and its quotient are canonical relative to one object of the finite-presentation comparison groupoid, with chosen transport along paths. | **O**; say **invariant of a chosen presentation, functorial along chosen comparison zigzags**. |
+| 47 | `strict visibility` versus `homological/intrinsic visibility` | title, `main.tex:58`; explicit contrast `sec_homological_visibility_intrinsic.tex:233` | Informal/theorem-defined | "Strict" uses all cocycle values on 2-chains (`H_alpha`); "homological" uses only the image of the induced map on 2-cycles/homology (`K_omega`). | **C**; "strict" and "intrinsic" have strong categorical meanings unrelated to this distinction. +| 48 | `pure-extension quotient`, `pure Ext contribution/residual/type` | abstract, `main.tex:70`; theorem `sec_homological_visibility_intrinsic.tex:117` | Theorem-defined | A quotient after which the pushed-forward `H^2` class lies in the `Ext^1(H_1,-)` kernel of the universal-coefficient map. | **C, severe**; a pure extension is a standard notion in abelian-group/module theory and is not what is meant. +| 49 | `character-blind obstruction/branch/case` | abstract, `main.tex:70`; equivalence theorem `sec_homological_visibility_intrinsic.tex:318` | Informal but mathematically characterized | A nonzero class with `ev_omega=0`, so every character is class-admissible; equivalently the class lies in the UCT `Ext` subgroup. | **O**; **nonzero class with vanishing `H_2` evaluation**. +| 50 | `chain-level evaluation map` | `sec_homological_visibility_intrinsic.tex:216` | Formal | The homomorphism `C_2(N,Z)->A` obtained by linearly extending the values of the cocycle on oriented 2-simplices. | **A**; **cochain `alpha` viewed as a homomorphism on 2-chains** is standard. |
+| 51 | `intrinsic strictification code/budget` | `sec_homological_visibility_intrinsic.tex:617` | Formal; budget in following corollaries | The fiber-separating register for `A->A/K_omega`; optimal size is `|K_omega|` and logarithm is called a budget. | **C**; it is neither intrinsic outside the comparison groupoid nor a strictification. +| 52 | `hidden-state budget`, `strictification budget`, `uniform hidden budget` | `sec_gerbe_visible_strictification.tex:250`; later repeatedly | Informal/theorem-defined | `log_2` of a subgroup/fiber cardinality, interpreted as the minimum number of auxiliary bits needed by an injective set-theoretic encoding. | **C**; "state" suggests semantic states and "budget" suggests an operational coding model that is not supplied. +| 53 | `maximal collapse` | `sec_homological_visibility_intrinsic.tex:477`; criterion at line 729 | Informal/theorem-defined | The case `ev_omega` is onto, so `K_omega=A` and `A/K_omega=0`. | **O**; say **surjective homological evaluation** or **zero homological cokernel**. |
+| 54 | `branchwise intrinsic data` | `sec_introduction.tex:22`; formal `sec_branch_aggregation.tex:5` | Formal | A finite nonempty set of component sections, each with the same finite abelian band and a finite nerve representative, together with `K_v` and `A/K_v`. | **O**; **family of componentwise homological image subgroups**. +| 55 | `branch-sensitive visible quotient` | `sec_introduction.tex:22`; theorem `sec_branch_aggregation.tex:22` | Theorem-defined, not a definition environment | `A / intersection_v K_v`, equivalently the image of `A` in the product of the componentwise quotients; the component label may be used. | **O**, conceptually load-bearing. +| 56 | `branch-uniform visible quotient` | `sec_introduction.tex:22`; theorem `sec_branch_aggregation.tex:54` | Theorem-defined | `A / sum_v K_v`, detected by characters annihilating every `K_v`; the component label is forgotten. | **O**, conceptually load-bearing. +| 57 | `uniformly admissible characters` | `sec_branch_aggregation.tex:54-59` | Theorem-defined | `intersection_v Ann(K_v)`, the characters annihilating every componentwise image subgroup. | **O**; **common annihilator of the component image subgroups**. |

+| 60 | `branch-resolution code/budget` | `sec_branch_aggregation.tex:245` | Formal | A fiber-separating register for the map from the label-aware quotient to the common-character quotient; optimal register size is the kernel size. | **C** through `branch`, `resolution`, and `code`. +| 61 | `branch-preserving strictification code` | `sec_branch_aggregation.tex:338` | Formal | One common finite register that injectively separates every quotient map `A->A/K_v`; minimum size is `max_v |K_v|`. | **C**; say **common auxiliary register for the componentwise quotient maps**. |
+| 62 | `realization theorem`, `prescribed branch realization`, `realizable subgroup` | `sec_introduction.tex:22`; theorem `sec_branch_realization.tex:790` | Theorem statement/construction, no general definition | A synthetic construction of a one-state typed expansion whose componentwise evaluation maps have prescribed images. | **C** through model-theoretic "realization". +| 63 | `mixed realization` | abstract, `main.tex:70`; theorem `sec_branch_mixed_realization.tex:1` | Theorem-defined by construction | The same construction allowing both zero maps (neutral component gerbes) and nonzero maps (non-neutral ones). | **C**; in model theory this sounds like simultaneous realization of types. +| 66 | `bouquet`, `bouquet site`, `bouquet good-cover family` | abstract, `main.tex:70`; precise construction `sec_branch_bouquet_resolution.tex:136` | Base space and site constructed in theorem | A finite model of `wedge_{j=1}^beta S^2`, its barycentric open-star good covers, and the pullback site generated by their intersections. | **A** for **bouquet = wedge sum**.
